name: word-behind-subject
what_you_see: A photograph fills the screen and one huge word, 18 to 26vw, runs behind the person or object in it, so the letters pass behind a shoulder and come out the other side. It reads like a magazine cover. Three layers: the picture, the word, the same picture's subject cut out on top, each moving at its own speed on scroll.
recipe: `composition.md` 1. Make the top layer with scripts/cutout.swift, or render on a transparent ground.
transfer: Any business with one person or object worth looking at. A baker behind the word Bread, a van in front of a town's name.

name: window-that-opens
what_you_see: Near-empty ground, a small picture in the centre, one word either side like a sentence with a photograph for a middle word. Scrolling pins it and the window grows until the picture fills the screen and the words slide away. You feel you walked through it.
transfer: Use the moment the work begins: a door opening, a kitchen before service, a bench at dawn.

name: pictures-inside-the-sentence
what_you_see: A headline at 6 to 8vw where small photographs sit in the line at cap height, between the words, growing open as it enters. The eye keeps stopping to look and the sentence feels made for this business.
transfer: Macro crops of what the business touches: oak, flour, thread, a stamp.

name: numeral-made-of-picture
what_you_see: One number as large as the window, 30 to 40vw, with a photograph showing through the digits. The number stops being data and becomes an object.
transfer: A price, a founding year, a count of customers. Choose a dark or saturated picture.

name: film-strip
what_you_see: A pinned scene where scrolling down walks you sideways past pictures of different widths, 26 to 50vw, each with one short line such as a time of day. It starts with a large title as the first frame. Ordinary steps become a walk past a wall.
transfer: A day at the business, the journey of an order, the life of a loan.

name: image-follows-the-list
what_you_see: A list set huge, 5 to 7vw, on a plain ground. Hover a row and a photograph opens beside the cursor and trails it with a little lag while other rows fade back. Plain words at rest, a gallery under the hand.
transfer: Services, past jobs, news, products. Give phones a small picture in each row.

name: columns-take-turns
what_you_see: Four to six tall pictures side by side at full height, each a sliver with a name running up its edge. The one you hover or tap swells to take most of the row and its caption slides in.
transfer: People, branches, products or chapters.

name: notes-hung-on-the-picture
what_you_see: One big photograph with small notes placed right on the things in it, joined by thin lines: a price on the shelf, a sentence beside a tool. The picture becomes a diagram of the business, and notes can arrive one at a time on scroll.
recipe: `composition.md` 8 and Notes on a picture in `components.md`.
transfer: Anything with a workplace: a counter, a kitchen, a surgery, a van.

name: bleeding-headline
what_you_see: A heading so big it runs off the screen, cropped on purpose, with a picture butted hard against it. Scroll slides it sideways so the rest arrives. The page feels larger than the window.
transfer: Works on a type-led page too. The word must still read.

name: overlapping-prints
what_you_see: Two or three pictures of different sizes laid over each other and over the heading, like prints on a table, drifting at different speeds. Nothing sits in a neat cell.
transfer: Any set of three good photographs.

name: colour-field-cutout
what_you_see: A full-screen flat field of the brand colour with one cut-out person or object on it, large and bleeding off the bottom edge, with type set against the empty side. An ordinary photograph suddenly looks like a campaign.
transfer: One person or product from the set, cut out with scripts/cutout.swift.

name: odometer-answer
what_you_see: A huge number that rolls digit by digit like a machine as you drag a slider tied to your own figure. The result is about you, and it changes as fast as you can move.
transfer: Interest earned, time saved, weight of flour, miles covered.

name: sentence-form
what_you_see: A line of display type with blanks in it. The visitor completes the sentence in place, and it answers them.
recipe: A form that is a sentence in `components.md`.
transfer: Any enquiry: I need a table for two on Friday.

name: drag-across-two
what_you_see: A handle dragged across two pictures of the same place, before and after.
transfer: Before and after a repair, a clean, a renovation, a month of bookkeeping.

name: deck-you-throw
what_you_see: A fanned stack of cards. Drag the top one and it leans, flick it and it flies off while the rest rise. Reading quotes becomes a small game.
transfer: Quotes, tips, tickets, recipes.

name: day-you-scrub
what_you_see: A 24-hour ruler with a thin playhead you drag. As the hour changes, the sentence below changes, and a picture can change with it.
transfer: What happens at the bakery at 4am, the clinic at noon, the depot at dusk.

name: words-light-as-you-read
what_you_see: A long sentence set at 4 to 6vw, almost invisible, each word coming up as it passes the reading line. A paragraph becomes a scene.
transfer: The one sentence that says what the business believes.

name: sheets-slide-over
what_you_see: Full-height scenes stack like sheets. Each slides over the last, which sinks back and dims as it is covered.
transfer: Three chapters of a story, each with its own ground.

name: ground-takes-over
what_you_see: The whole page changes colour as a scene arrives, with no edge between them, going dark for one scene and back.
transfer: One dark chapter past the middle of the page.

name: speed-aware-marquee
what_you_see: One line of huge type crossing the screen, slow at rest and faster as you scroll, as though attached to your hand. Named places or trades rather than logos.
transfer: Towns served, trades served, ingredients.

name: walk-down-a-tall-portrait
what_you_see: One dark section 2970px tall (3.3 viewports at 900px) holds a single portrait 3008x3300px, more than twice the viewport width, so the page only ever shows head, neck and shoulders. A 110px white headline and five lines of body sit centred on the empty blue backdrop above the head, in the top 60% of the first screen. The ear cup and then the face pass through the frame with no text on them for about 1.5 viewports (y=3480 to 4560). The model's dark pleated shirt then fills the frame edge to edge and becomes the ground for three small white paragraphs, in a 590px column starting 29% from the left. The picture moves at plain scroll speed, so the whole effect comes from the size of the photo and where the copy is placed on it.
recipe: section{position:relative;height:330vh;overflow:hidden;background:linear-gradient(#59798e 0%,#6b8da8 70%,#000 100%)} .portrait{position:absolute;top:0;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);width:209vw;height:auto;max-width:none}. Sample the gradient stops from the photo's own top and bottom so no section edge shows. Place text with absolute top values in vh read off the photo: headline at about 12vh on the empty backdrop, nothing from 110vh to 210vh, small paragraphs from 225vh on the dark area, colour #f5f5f7, 17px/1.4, width 590px. No scroll code at all.
transfer: A bakery shoots one tall photo of a baker in a dark apron, sets the headline on the plain wall above the head and the opening hours on the apron. A dentist can do the same with a dark scrub top and one phone photo.
depends_on: A vertically composed portrait with generous empty backdrop above and a large dark garment below, at least 3000px wide. Engines seen: no global GSAP, no Lenis, no WebGL or canvas.
why: A template gives text and image separate boxes, while here each block of copy is placed by reading the photo, on the sky or the shirt, and the face is left alone.

name: leader-line-draws-to-the-feature
what_you_see: A macro of the ear cup fills the right 65% of the frame and a copy block sits at the left margin. A 1px grey line starts at the left margin above that copy and runs right across the empty ground onto the product, ending in a tiny dot inside the physical button the copy describes. In 40px wheel steps the line is absent at y=7040, about 345px long at y=7080 and full length, about 885px, at y=7120. It then darkens from pale grey over the next two steps. The trigger point is when the line reaches about 77% of viewport height.
recipe: Wrapper position:relative holding copy and image. .line{position:absolute;left:0;top:<y>;height:1px;width:<x of feature as % of wrapper>;background:#86868b;transform:scaleX(0);transform-origin:left;opacity:.4;transition:transform .6s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1),opacity .6s .3s} .line::after{content:'';position:absolute;right:0;top:-2px;width:5px;height:5px;border-radius:50%;background:inherit}. IntersectionObserver with rootMargin '0px 0px -23% 0px' adds .in, which sets scaleX(1) and opacity 1. Duration is inferred: it finished within one 400ms step, so it runs on a trigger and is not scrubbed. Under reduced motion show it drawn.
transfer: A dentist labels one spot on an X-ray, or a bank labels one field on a statement, with a single line running from the sentence to the exact place on the picture.
depends_on: A photo with a clear small feature and clear space between it and the text. Express the end point as a percentage of the image so it survives resizing.
why: The line's end point is a coordinate on one particular photo, so it has to be authored for that picture.

name: frameless-macro-on-page-ground
what_you_see: The ear cup is shown so close that it exceeds the screen: it enters from the right edge, spans about 55% of the viewport width and is cropped by the viewport itself. It has no card or tile, because the cut-out sits directly on the page's own pale grey, so the object appears to rest on the page. Its metal stem drops about two-thirds of a viewport and stops on a 180px hairline, like a post standing on a shelf. The copy keeps to the left 40% in a narrow 320px column.
recipe: Cut the subject out to transparent WebP, or shoot on the exact page colour. section{position:relative;overflow:clip;background:#f5f5f7} img{position:absolute;right:-12vw;width:78vw;max-width:none}. The image edge must match the ground exactly. Copy: left 40%, max-width 320px. Stand any vertical part of the subject on a 1px rule 180px wide.
transfer: A bakery shows one loaf huge and cropped by the side of the screen on a page the same cream as the paper it was shot on. A window and a sheet of paper are enough.
depends_on: A sharp, high-resolution cut-out at about 2000px wide, and a page ground that matches it.
why: A template image slot always has a box, and this object has none, using the edge of the screen as its only crop.

name: scattered-tiles-with-held-space
what_you_see: Under a 48px question at top left, three product tiles sit off any shared column line: 589x589 at x=8, 589x441 at x=843 starting 144px higher, and one 350px wide at x=724 starting 162px above the first tile's bottom edge. Each tile is a soft grey gradient that fades into the page at its top, with no shadow or border and a small radius. Large cells stay open between them, including 246px between the first two. Each tile has only a 14px mono label under its bottom left corner, so the eye zigzags as it would across items laid on a table.
recipe: On a 24-column grid at 1440 (60px per column, 8px page padding): tile A grid-column:1/11, margin-top:145px; tile B grid-column:15/25; tile C grid-column:13/19, margin-top:-162px. Tile background: linear-gradient(#f4f4f4,#cfd2d5), radius 8px, no shadow. Caption: mono 14px, underlined. Below 900px fall back to two columns and keep one offset of 80px.
transfer: A bakery lays out three loaves at three sizes, one big, one tall, one small, under one plain question, like goods on a counter.
depends_on: Three to five single-subject shots on matching backdrops, and a client willing to leave cells empty.
why: Sizes and offsets are hand placed for these items, whereas grid templates force equal columns and shared top edges.

name: film-title-card-over-a-macro
what_you_see: The hero is an inset film player, 1391px wide with 25px side margins, starting at y=154 under a cream band, with a real scrubber and timestamp along its bottom edge. It opens on an extreme close-up of a dented brass horn carried at hip height, with no faces. The only words are a title about 273px wide, 20% of the frame, in tracked serif capitals with one lowercase italic connecting word. It sits centred at 52% of frame height over the dark trousers beside the horn, so it barely touches the subject. The title appears to be burned into the film (inferred: the hero is an embedded video iframe and those words are not in the page DOM).
recipe: Frame: margin:0 25px;aspect-ratio:16/9. Title: about 1.7vw (24px at 1440), letter-spacing:.24em, uppercase, connective word italic lowercase with letter-spacing:.02em, width no more than 20% of the frame, placed on the darkest part of the shot. Keep real player controls on show and leave the viewer in charge of playback.
transfer: A dentist films 30 seconds of hands laying out instruments and gives it a four-word title, small and tracked, like the start of a documentary.
depends_on: A real short film with a strong macro shot. Engines seen: none, the hero is an embedded player. No global GSAP, no Lenis, no canvas.
why: Templates lay a big headline and button over a looped background video, while this treats the hero as a short film with its own title card and controls.

name: unequal-diptych-day-and-night
what_you_see: Two pictures stand side by side at 915x570 and 439x577, a ratio of about 2:1, 37px apart with tops within 4px of each other. The left one is a wide daylight colonnade reflected in a pool, and the right one is a slim night scene of a lit globe on dark water: same family, opposite mood. Under each sits a tiny label, a 19.6px serif title, two lines of 14px copy and a text link. The same split returns lower on the page at y=2791, so it works as the page's rhythm and not a one-off.
recipe: display:grid;grid-template-columns:2.08fr 1fr;gap:37px;padding:0 25px. Both images height:570px;object-fit:cover. Under each: label 10px tracked caps, h3 20px/1.3 serif weight 400, p 14px/1.5, underlined link 13px. Choose the pair by contrast of light: the wide one is day, the narrow one is night or a detail.
transfer: A bakery pairs a wide daylight shot of the shop with a narrow shot of the oven glowing at 4am.
depends_on: Two photos of the same subject matter with opposite light.
why: Template rows split evenly into halves or thirds and would never pair a wide day picture with a slim night one.

name: caption-scale-headlines
what_you_see: On a page with a 1391px film and 915px photographs, the largest live text anywhere is 31px, a light serif used once. Section titles are 19.6 to 24px and links are 13px, on warm cream. No page text overlaps an image, and every caption sits in the margin under its picture like a museum label. The ratio of picture width to title size is about 45 to 1.
recipe: Cap the scale at 31 / 24 / 19.6 / 14 / 13px. Top size weight 300, normal tracking. Warm cream ground, about #f3eee7. Text always under the image, never on it. Images keep full column width. Hard rule: no live text above about 2.2vw.
transfer: A private dentist or a law firm uses large honest photographs of the room and the people with 20px captions, which reads as confidence and not as shouting.
depends_on: Photography strong enough to carry all the page's attention. With weak photos this reads as empty.
why: Templates default to a very large hero heading, and holding a whole page at caption scale is a judgement no preset makes.

name: live-conditions-tile
what_you_see: At the bottom left of the hero film sits a translucent sage tile 400x220px, flush to the hero's left and bottom edges. Its left half holds a drawn sun, the current temperature at about 34px and a link to watch the garden live. Its right half is a booking menu of six plain links. The number was 14 degrees in one run of mine and 15 in another minutes later, so the hero reports a fact about today and not a slogan.
recipe: .hero{position:relative} .tile{position:absolute;left:0;bottom:0;width:400px;height:220px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;background:rgba(108,124,115,.85);color:#fff}. Fetch the value from a free source at load, such as Open-Meteo with no key, and hide the number on failure rather than show a stale one. The link goes to a webcam or a live status page.
transfer: A bakery shows 'sourdough out at 7:40, 12 left'. A dentist shows the next free appointment. A bank branch shows the current queue time.
depends_on: One number that is really true right now, and a fallback for when it is unavailable. Engines seen: none, plain video.
why: A template cannot know the weather at your gate, so this tile only makes sense for one physical place.

name: shot-on-white-needs-no-cutout
what_you_see: Directly under the hero, two hens stand on nothing: a 572x365px photo shot on pure white and placed on a pure white page, so the picture has no visible edge. A soft floor shadow holds them down. They sit left of a short intro, at the size another site would give an icon row or stats. Further down a flat lay of plates and linen on white does the same thing and runs off the right edge of the page. The file is an ordinary photo with no transparency, so the cut-out effect comes from the shoot.
recipe: Shoot the subject on white paper or a white wall. Push the background to exactly #fff in any editor and export as WebP or JPG with no alpha. Place on background:#fff with no border or radius, width about 40vw, text alongside and vertically centred. Check the join with an eyedropper. Keep the soft shadow.
transfer: A bakery shoots one bun on white paper by a window. A dentist shoots a toothbrush. A bank shoots a rubber-banded stack of statements. It costs a phone and a sheet of paper.
depends_on: A subject that can be shot on white and a page ground of the same white.
why: The picture is one specific animal from the real farm where a template has an icon, and its edge is removed by photography and not by a mask.

name: product-part-as-punctuation
what_you_see: A macro of a black bike frame fills an inset plate, with tubes cutting diagonally across a white-to-black gradient. The two-character model name is 280px white grotesque at normal weight, from x=127 to x=455, and immediately after its last digit comes the bike's glowing red tail-light, between y=395 and y=500. The light reads as a third glyph, like a full stop. The first letter crosses the spokes and the digit's foot rests on the top tube, so the word feels set into the machine. The phone frame keeps the same pairing, so this was composed for both crops.
recipe: Crop the photo so one bright feature falls about 37% across and 49% down. h1{position:absolute;left:8.8vw;top:<feature top minus 4vw>;font-size:19.4vw;line-height:1;font-weight:400;color:#fff}. Keep a gap of about 3vw between the last glyph and the feature. Size type and image in vw and fix object-position so the two stay locked. Serve a separate portrait crop on phones that keeps the pair intact.
transfer: A bank sets a large 0% with a coin as the next character. A bakery sets a price with a round bun as the full stop.
depends_on: A product with one saturated or bright feature and quiet space to its left. Engines seen: no global GSAP, no Lenis, no WebGL or canvas.
why: The text position is decided by one feature in one photograph, and a text slot cannot know where the tail-light is.

name: abstract-benefit-as-a-lit-scene
what_you_see: Security is explained by one night photograph with no icons. A bike stands in a dark field under a single cone of blue light falling from above, a patch of lit green grass at its wheels and dim animal shapes around it. The frame is picked out by rim light. A 48px headline and two lines of small copy sit in the left 35% on the dark, level with the bike. The plate is 1424x801px, about 90% of the frame, with no overlays or boxes.
recipe: Plan the shot around one light source. Plate radius 8px, image object-fit:cover, text absolute at left:8.8vw;top:52%, h2 48px/1.1 white, p 16px/1.4. The dark ground gives contrast so no scrim is needed. Without a shoot, dim a normal photo with filter:brightness(.35) and add radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 0,rgba(140,190,255,.5),transparent 60%) with mix-blend-mode:screen.
transfer: A bank explains fraud protection with one photo of a front door at night under a porch lamp, in place of a shield icon.
depends_on: One staged photograph with a single light source. Engines seen: none.
why: A feature block is normally an icon, heading and blurb, whereas this stages the feature as a small story with a place and a time.

name: interface-on-its-real-mount
what_you_see: The app section is one grey panel 1200px wide on a white page. The interface is not in a floating phone: a dark phone 820px wide is clamped to real handlebars that run out of both sides of the panel, cut by its edges, with a stem dropping out of its bottom edge. The screen shows a speed dial, ride stats and a dark map. Above it sit an 80px title, a small button and four one-line icon features.
recipe: Panel: max-width:1200px;margin:auto;background:#f0f0f0;overflow:hidden. Image: transparent render or photo with the mount wider than the panel, so it runs out of the crop on both sides; img{width:100%;display:block}. Device about 68% of panel width, real interface on screen.
transfer: A bakery shows its order page on the tablet on the real counter next to the till. A dentist shows booking on the reception screen.
depends_on: A real or rendered view of the interface where it is actually used.
why: Templates float a device mockup in space, whereas here the device is in its working position and the setting explains the product.

name: name-and-price-on-one-horizon
what_you_see: Three soft-knit figures stand shoulder to shoulder across the middle 60% of the frame. On one horizontal at 50% of the viewport, the product name sits at the far left in 44px from x=33 to x=363, crossing the neck of the left figure by about 130px. At the far right on the same line sit a 14px deposit price and a dark pill button. Nothing else is on screen except the nav, so the words form a horizon running through the group.
recipe: .hero{position:relative;height:100vh} .horizon{position:absolute;left:32px;right:32px;top:50%;transform:translateY(-50%);display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center}. Left: h1 as a two-tone line, 44px. Right: 14px price and a 36px tall pill. Centre the subject group so its neck or waist line meets that horizon.
transfer: A bakery shows a shelf of three loaves with the name left and price and order button right, on one line through the middle of the loaves.
depends_on: A group of subjects with a clear horizontal band at mid-height, and very few words.
why: A template stacks heading, text and button in a column, whereas here they are split to opposite edges along one line with the subject between them.

name: subject-dissolves-into-ground
what_you_see: The figures' torsos are never cut by the section edge. Over the lower 35% of the photo they fade into the pale paper colour, so they seem to rise out of mist. The panel then ends in a hard horizontal cut against the next full-bleed photo, a blue backdrop that starts at a man's hair with no gap. One soft edge and one hard edge meet on the same line. Whether the fade is baked or masked could not be determined.
recipe: .figure{-webkit-mask-image:linear-gradient(#000 62%,transparent 100%);mask-image:linear-gradient(#000 62%,transparent 100%)} over a background equal to the page ground, or bake the fade into the file. Set the next section with margin:0 so it butts directly against it.
transfer: A bank's team portrait fades at the waist into the page colour, so a phone crop never cuts people awkwardly.
depends_on: Subjects that can fade at waist height and a flat ground colour.
why: A template photo ends at its box, whereas this photo's lower edge is art-directed into the page ground.

name: title-fitted-per-item
what_you_see: Each film in the hero gets a title measured to its own length so the longest line nearly fills the 1440px viewport: 225px for a four-word title on two lines, 400px for a two-word title, 344px for the third. Line-height is 0.8 and tracking -0.05em, so the lines almost touch. On two-line titles the first line is flush left and the second flush right. Awkward letter pairs are kerned by hand in the markup, with -0.124em after a Y and -0.05em after a T. The white type fills the lower third of the still and runs across shoulders and jackets, in front of the people in the shot.
recipe: Render each title at 100px in a hidden span, measure width w, then --fs = 100*(innerWidth-40)/w, clamped 120 to 400px. h2{font-size:var(--fs);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.05em;font-weight:485} with a variable font. Long titles split into two balanced lines, .line:nth-child(2){text-align:right}. Kerning map {Y:-.124,T:-.05}: wrap the following letters in <span style='display:inline-block;margin-inline-start:-.124em'>. Measure after document.fonts.ready and again from a ResizeObserver.
transfer: A bakery's daily special fills the screen width whatever its length: one short word enormous, a long name smaller. The width stays constant and the size carries the surprise.
depends_on: A heavy-enough grotesque, ideally variable, and stills with calm lower thirds. Engines seen: no global GSAP, no Lenis, no WebGL or canvas.
why: Template headings use one fixed size, while here every title gets its own size, so the rhythm changes from item to item.

name: sticky-stack-wipes-the-title
what_you_see: Three full-width film stills are stacked. Each slide is 836px tall in a 900px viewport and sticks at top:0, so the top 64px of the next film always shows at the bottom under a 6px white rule. As you scroll, the next slide rises over the current one, and frames at 360px steps show that rule cutting horizontally through the giant title, leaving the tops of its letters above the line. The title neither fades nor moves: it is simply wiped by the next picture. The stack's container is 2524px tall, so three slides pass in about 1.8 viewports of scroll.
recipe: .slide{position:sticky;top:0;height:calc(100vh - 64px);border-top:6px solid #fff;overflow:hidden} with DOM order giving each later slide the upper layer. Title absolute at bottom:54px. Last slide position:relative so it scrolls away. No JavaScript at all.
transfer: A dentist's three treatments stack as full-height photos, each with one big word, and each scroll wipes the last word away.
depends_on: Stills with faces in the upper half, so the title never covers them. CSS sticky only.
why: Template carousels swap slides on a timer, while here the change is a physical overlap the reader drives, with the title as the thing that gets cut.

name: product-flipbook-loop
what_you_see: A book lies open on a pale grey panel, 944x673px, shot from above with its real page edges and a soft shadow. It does not stay still: the spread changes by hard cut on its own, including one frame of the closed cover. With the page parked at y=3240, eight screenshots gave six different frames, and the scroll position and image source did not change. It is one animated WebP file with no video or canvas, so it runs on time and not on scroll. Hovering a nearby record sleeve produced no change, so the interest here is only the loop.
recipe: Shoot 8 to 12 spreads from a fixed overhead camera with the same light. Export as animated WebP at about 700ms per frame, quality 80, about 1000px wide: img2webp -d 700 -q 80 *.jpg -o flip.webp. . No JavaScript.
transfer: A bakery flips through its recipe booklet. A dentist flips through a patient guide. A bank flips through a welcome pack. Ten phone photos.
depends_on: A physical product with an inside: a book, a menu, a box, a folder. A phone on a tripod is enough. Frame interval inferred from the samples.
why: A product block shows one still, whereas this shows the inside of the product as a quick loop that costs a single image slot.

name: offer-name-as-a-made-object
what_you_see: The lower half of the footer holds a rendered chrome word, its letters extruded in steep perspective and growing in height from left to right. It runs from 34% of the width to the right edge, rises to about 44% of viewport height and its feet sit on a hairline rule that crops it. To its left is a two-line offer of about 44px and one solid white button. Against flat black it is the only 3D object on the page, placed in what is normally dead space.
recipe: Model the word in Blender or Spline with brushed metal at steep perspective, export transparent PNG about 1000x400. Footer lower band: display:grid;grid-template-columns:33% 67%;align-items:end;border-bottom:1px solid #444;overflow:hidden. Keep the link columns above it small, 16 to 18px.
transfer: A bakery spells its loyalty scheme in biscuit letters, bakes them and photographs them. A real object beats a render here.
depends_on: One offer worth naming and a render or real object.
why: Template footers are link columns, and this one ends the page with a made object carrying an offer.

name: listing-set-on-the-facade
what_you_see: A full-bleed photo of a real brick theatre with a red awning fills about 88% of the viewport height. Its lower third carries the whole listing directly on the brickwork: a 96px two-line title at the left, small stacked credits, a synopsis in 14px white, and a solid white ticket button at the far right. The bottom of each block lines up along one band. Because the building is the actual venue, the picture is doing the job of the address.
recipe: section{position:relative;height:88vh} img{width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover}. .band{position:absolute;left:22px;right:22px;bottom:20px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:320px 160px 1fr auto;gap:24px;align-items:end;color:#fff}. h2 96px/.87, letter-spacing:-.034em. Credits 11px mono. Synopsis 14px/1.4, max-width 56ch. Darken only the lower third: linear-gradient(transparent 55%,rgba(0,0,0,.45)).
transfer: A dentist uses a straight-on photo of the shopfront and sets hours, phone number and a booking button across the pavement in the picture.
depends_on: A real photo of the actual place with a busy but dark lower third.
why: A template would put these details in a card beside the picture, while here the listing lies on the building it refers to.

name: pinned-title-over-a-passing-photo
what_you_see: A 1440x1865px photo shows green wooden cubes and painted balls hanging above blue cloth that meets an ochre floor. A serif capitals headline, effectively 126px and fitted to 1372px of the 1440px width, holds still near the bottom of the viewport while the photograph slides up behind it for at least 960px of scroll. A small caption holds still at the top. The objects seem to fall past the words, the ochre floor rises behind the letters, then the title is released and leaves with the picture's bottom edge. White type stays legible on both the blue and the ochre.
recipe: section{position:relative;height:226vh} img{position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:auto}. .title{position:sticky;top:calc(100vh - 190px);padding:0 34px}. Fit to width: set font-size:20px, measure the span, then transform:scale(containerWidth/spanWidth);transform-origin:left, which is how the site does it with a measured scale of 6.32. Serif capitals, weight 400, white. The site's pin is script driven under smooth scroll (inferred, no sticky in the title's chain); sticky gives the same result.
transfer: A bakery shoots one tall photo of flour falling onto a bench, and three plain words stay still while it passes behind them.
depends_on: A tall photo of at least two viewports with a colour change or an eye path running down it. Engine seen: Lenis smooth scroll, two videos elsewhere, no global GSAP, no WebGL.
why: Heroes normally fix the picture and move the text or move both, while here the headline is the still point and the photograph is the motion.

name: cover-at-holding-size
what_you_see: The home page opens with no full-bleed picture. On plain white, a two-line centred serif title of about 38px sits above the magazine cover at true proportions, about 318x405px, which is 45% of viewport height. Two tiny links sit under it, and only the last 48px of the viewport shows a sliver of the next image. A publication with huge photos shows its first view at roughly the size you would hold it.
recipe: .hero{min-height:100vh;display:grid;place-items:center;background:#fff;text-align:center;padding-bottom:48px} h1{font:400 38px/1.1 serif} img{width:22vw;box-shadow:none}. Links 12px under the object. Let the next section start at calc(100vh - 48px) so it peeks.
transfer: A bank shows the card at actual size on white. A bakery shows one loaf at the size it sits on the counter.
depends_on: A designed physical object with real presence at small size.
why: A template hero is a full-width image, and shrinking the strongest asset to life size on white goes against that instinct.

name: private-glyph-per-entry
what_you_see: Every project in the index has a 38px black square holding a tiny white pictogram drawn for that one building, its silhouette or plan reduced to a mark. The square sits above a right-aligned caption in the left gutter, with the project name in about 13px and the location in about 11px grey capitals. There were 263 of these icons in the DOM at load. They work like a private alphabet, and the column of black squares gives the long page its beat.
recipe: For each item, a 52x52 SVG, white on black, shown at 38x38. Caption block: text-align:right, name 13px, place 11px uppercase #888, sitting in the gutter 11px left of the image. Generate glyphs by tracing each subject's silhouette or plan to a single shape inside the square.
transfer: A bakery draws one tiny stamp per loaf from its slash pattern and uses it on the bag too. A dentist draws one per treatment.
depends_on: A list of real things, and an afternoon per dozen to draw them. Engine seen: Lenis smooth scroll. No global GSAP, no WebGL, no video.
why: A library icon set cannot do this, because each glyph encodes one specific building.

name: cycling-search-hint
what_you_see: At the right of the fixed nav, next to a small magnifier, one grey capitals word changes by itself. Across frames about a second apart it read a country, a building type, a theme, and a project status. It never says 'search'. Each word teaches one dimension you can search by, so the field demonstrates its own range without instruction.
recipe: const hints=[a place,a type,a theme,a status]; every 1800ms swap the text with a .25s crossfade. Stop and clear on focus. Keep a constant aria-label so screen readers do not hear it change. Pause under prefers-reduced-motion. 12px uppercase, tracking .04em, #999. Interval is inferred from frames: the word changed roughly every one to two seconds.
transfer: A dentist's search cycles a treatment, a symptom and a day. A bakery's cycles a loaf, an allergy and a day.
depends_on: A search with more than one real dimension.
why: A static placeholder says only that search exists, while this one shows what the search knows.

name: logo-rides-the-curtain
what_you_see: Load starts on a full black screen with a small white logo at centre, held until about 1.7s. The logo then travels up and to the left as the black sheet lifts: at about 2.5s the black covers only the top 21% with the logo near its top left corner, and the index is already in place underneath. By about 3.2s the sheet has gone. There is no spinner and no fade, because the page was already there and the curtain simply leaves.
recipe: <div class='curtain'> .curtain{position:fixed;inset:0;background:#000;z-index:10}, logo absolutely centred. After fonts and first images, or 1500ms at most: curtain transform:translateY(-100%) over .9s cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1), and logo translate(-600px,-378px) over the same time. Skip on repeat views with sessionStorage. Timing curve inferred from four frames.
transfer: A bakery's one-second screen with its stamp lifts like a shop shutter. Keep it under 1.5 seconds.
depends_on: A mark that reads at small size, and the discipline to run it once per visit.
why: Template loaders spin on a blank screen, whereas this does one stage gesture and drops the reader straight into the content.

name: word-sandwiched-in-the-picture
what_you_see: A 360px black-weight navy word sits across a sunny full-bleed house photo, from about x=210 to x=1255 and y=126 to y=486. Sky and cloud are behind the letters while the roofline, the dormer and the branches of a yellow tree pass in front. The first letter is half eaten by the gable and leaves, and the foot of the last letter is cut by the tree on the right. Nothing else is on screen except a 13px scroll hint at top centre. The word becomes part of the landscape, about as tall as the house.
recipe: Two PNGs at 1440x1204: back (full photo) and front (same photo with the sky masked out, roof and foliage kept, leaves feathered by hand). .hero{position:relative;height:100vh;overflow:hidden} back, h1 and front all absolute inset:0, front on top and aria-hidden, both images object-fit:cover. h1{text-align:center;top:14vh;font-weight:900;font-size:25vw;line-height:1}, colour a deep navy sampled from the photo's shadows. Serve a tighter crop on phones.
transfer: A bakery sets its name behind a row of loaves on a shelf. A bank sets its town's name behind the real skyline. Free subject cut-out tools make the mask a ten-minute job.
depends_on: A photo with clean sky and a hard skyline, a short heavy word, and a careful mask. Engine seen: Framer site build. No global GSAP, no Lenis, no WebGL.
why: It needs a hand-masked foreground layer made for this exact photo and this exact word.

name: hero-collapses-into-the-sentence
what_you_see: On scroll the hero stays pinned while its frame shrinks towards the centre and the photo inside it keeps zooming in. At 360px of scroll the frame is about 60% wide and shows a dormer close-up, and at 720px it is about 21% wide. By then a centred statement is visible behind it, a label above, two lines of 18px text broken by the small picture covering their middle, and a link below. By about 960px the picture is a point inside the sentence and the line reads whole. Measured: outer clip scales 1 to 0 and inner image 1 to 4, both linear over 900px of scroll.
recipe:
...

. .pin{position:sticky;top:0;height:100vh;display:grid;place-items:center} .frame{position:absolute;inset:0;overflow:hidden}. On scroll: p=clamp(scrollY/innerHeight,0,1); frame.style.transform='scale('+(1-p)+')'; inner.style.transform='scale('+(1+3*p)+')'; hide the frame at p=1. The product of the two scales rises to about 1.33 near p=.4 before falling, which gives the push-in. The text never moves. Under reduced motion drop the pin.
transfer: A bakery's full-screen oven door closes down to a small picture inside one plain sentence about bread. One image and a few lines of script.
depends_on: A hero photo that still reads at 4x, and a short statement. Eight lines of JS or a scroll-linked animation.
why: A stock hero scrolls off or fades, whereas here the biggest thing on the page shrinks to a point inside the smallest text.

name: wordmark-at-building-scale
what_you_see: Between the project grid and the drawing, the company name runs as one line of 400px heavy navy type, 3610px long per copy, with three copies in a row, cropped by both edges of the viewport. Only about six letters fit at once, so you read the name over time. It keeps drifting left when idle, at about 74px per second as measured, and moves much faster during scrolling, covering 424px over 200px of scroll on the fastest stretch. The link between scroll speed and drift is inferred from those measurements.
recipe: h2{font-weight:900;font-size:400px;line-height:1;white-space:nowrap;will-change:transform}, three copies in a flex row. rAF loop: x -= dt*.074 + Math.abs(scrollDelta)*2; if x < -copyWidth then x += copyWidth. Use once per page only. Reduced motion: static, single copy.
transfer: A bakery's one word at 30vw crosses slowly between two sections. Use it once, as a pause.
depends_on: A short strong name and a heavy typeface.
why: Stock marquees are small logo strips at constant speed, whereas this is a word at the scale of the buildings, tied to the reader's own movement.

name: hand-drawing-among-the-photos
what_you_see: After a run of photographs the page switches register to a hand-inked axonometric drawing of the development. Neighbouring houses are left as bare outlines while the new buildings and trees carry blue, grey and green washes. It runs about 85% of the viewport width on the same paper ground with no frame, so it sits like a plan on a drafting table. The only words are a 13px caption near its top left. It shows how the plots connect, which no photograph could.
recipe: Transparent PNG or SVG. img{display:block;width:85vw;margin:0 auto} on a warm paper ground, with mix-blend-mode:multiply if the scan has a white ground. Caption absolute at top left, 13px. Colour only the subject and leave the surroundings as line.
transfer: A bakery draws a cutaway of its oven. A dentist draws a plan of the practice showing the step-free route. Colour only what matters.
depends_on: One real drawing. A pen and a scan are enough; the hand is the point.
why: It is a drawing of this specific site, which stock cannot supply and for which templates have no slot.

name: cast-shadow-is-the-page
what_you_see: The home page is effectively one image: a product on a pale floor, lit from above, throwing a black shadow straight down the screen for almost the full 5856px length. Technically it is four square 1440x1440 tiles stacked without a seam. The product sits in the first viewport on black, the floor brightens by about y=900, and the shadow widens as you go until the light floor is two thin strips at the sides near y=4200, and then gone. There are no sections and nothing else on the page but three small blocks of text and the header.
recipe: Render or compose a 1:4 image and slice it into four squares up to 2048px. img{display:block;width:100%;aspect-ratio:1;margin:0} on body{background:#000}, lazy-load all but the first. Text absolute at chosen y values as a percentage of the page. Light from directly overhead at a low angle.
transfer: A bakery's page is one long photo of a flour trail down a bench. A dentist's is a line of floss down the screen. The picture is the structure.
depends_on: A 3D render, or one long subject shot from above and stitched. Engines seen: none, static images only. No global GSAP, no Lenis, no canvas.
why: Templates are built from sections, and this page has none, only one continuous picture whose lighting sets the length of the scroll.

name: copy-in-the-cast-shadow
what_you_see: The buy block is set in the darkest part of the shadow, at about y=1240 to y=1370, centred, in 40px white capitals of a rounded techno face: a slogan, a price and an outlined button. No panel or scrim is needed because the shadow gives full contrast. Its soft edges frame the 315px wide block against the bright floor on both sides, about 95px clear either side. The block looks lit by the same scene, because the dark behind it is real.
recipe: Absolute at left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);top:<y in image>. font-size:2.755vw (39.7px at 1440);line-height:1.11;text-transform:uppercase;color:#fff. Button border:1px solid #fff;border-radius:4px;padding:0 40px. Use vw for type so the block stays inside the shadow when the image scales.
transfer: A bakery sets a price in the shadow of a rolling pin. A bank sets a rate in the shadow of a doorway.
depends_on: A shot with a dense, wide shadow. Low window light on a phone photo can give this.
why: The text's legibility comes from the lighting in the photo and not from an overlay.

name: scroll-scrubbed-dolly-into-the-product
what_you_see: The first screen is a wide photographic valley with a tiny desk and laptop in the lower middle, and over about 1,350px of scroll the camera pushes in without a cut. At 500px the desk fills the width, at 1,000px the laptop screen fills about 75% of the frame and the dashboard is legible, and at about 1,300px the surroundings are gone and only the dark interface remains on a dark ground. The headline, form and legal pill fade out by about 500px while a sticky 1440x900 stage holds under the nav. I read the video clock while scrolling: 0s at 0px, 2.36s at 500px, 4.72s at 1,000px, on a paused 6.4s clip, so it is a true scrub. Page height then drops from 13,033px to 11,683px and scrollY jumps back, so the track appears to be removed after one pass and the move does not replay (removal inferred).
recipe: Outer track height calc(100vh + 1350px). Inside it position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh; overflow: hidden. Muted video with object-fit: cover, preload auto, encoded all-keyframe (ffmpeg -g 1) or seeking stutters. In requestAnimationFrame set video.currentTime = progress * duration, about 0.0047s per px of scroll, easing toward the target by 0.15 per frame. Overlay text opacity = 1 - progress / 0.37. Mask the top of the video with a linear-gradient from transparent at 10% to opaque so it sinks into the page ground. End the clip on a frame colour-matched to the next section. Under prefers-reduced-motion show a poster and skip the track.
transfer: A dentist films one gimbal walk from the street door to the chair; a bakery pushes in from the shop window to the crumb of one loaf. One real unbroken 6-second move, shot on a phone, is enough.
depends_on: One continuous clip from wide shot to screen (3D render, AI video, or a drone plus macro shot), all-keyframe encoding, native sticky. No global GSAP, Lenis or THREE on the page; the scrub drives a plain video element.
why: The section is one planned shot whose last frame is the next section of the page, and no template ships a camera move that ends inside your own product.

name: tiny-subject-with-type-in-the-empty-sky
what_you_see: The desk and chair take about 23% of the frame width and sit between 58% and 84% of its height, centred on a grass ridge, with valley, mist and pink-grey sky filling everything else. The 49px headline, 20px subline and a pill email field stand centred in the top 40%, all in empty sky, and nothing overlaps the subject. A river runs up the centre axis behind the laptop and points back toward the form, so the eye moves between product and action along a line inside the picture. The photo runs full-bleed under a translucent nav and darkens toward its corners, which keeps white text readable without a flat scrim.
recipe: Hero 100vh, image object-fit: cover; object-position: center bottom. Keep all type inside the top 40%: centred column, max-width 620px, padding-top 96px. Subject centre at 70% of height and no wider than 25vw. Vignette: radial-gradient(ellipse 80% 70% at 50% 45%, transparent 55%, rgba(10,12,20,.55)). Headline 49px/1.1 weight 480 in rgba(255,255,255,.9). Field 400x48px pill in rgba(255,255,255,.12) with backdrop-filter: blur(12px).
transfer: Shoot the one chair, oven or counter from far back, so the place is the subject and the wall or sky above it becomes the headline area.
depends_on: A photo or composite with a small central subject, real empty headroom and one leading line.
why: The picture was composed for this one column of type, with its headroom, axis and subject scale decided by the words, which a stock crop never gives you.

name: figures-lifted-off-a-fading-document
what_you_see: A 496x330px pale tile holds a grey bill 308px wide, washed out to low contrast and dissolving into grain toward the tile's foot. Three white pills 44px tall, each with a small sparkle icon, float across the paper's edges carrying one value pulled from it: a name, a code, an amount. They are the only sharp, full-contrast things in the tile, and they overhang the sheet by 23 to 50px. The neighbouring tile uses the same contrast logic in depth, with one sharp dark card over two blurred cards stacked behind it.
recipe: Tile position: relative; aspect 3/2; background #ECEBE6. Document at 62% width, opacity .35, mask-image: linear-gradient(#000 45%, transparent 95%), plus an SVG feTurbulence noise layer at .25 with mix-blend-mode: multiply. Pills absolute, height 44px, radius 999px, white, box-shadow 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.08), 16px text, overhanging the sheet edge by 25 to 50px. Depth version: back cards filter: blur(8px), opacity .5, each 16px higher and 6% narrower. Motion on this tile was not observed; a 120ms stagger with an 8px rise is my suggestion.
transfer: A dentist fades an invoice and lifts out date, cost and what is covered; an accountant does it with a tax letter; a bank does it with a statement.
depends_on: A real-looking document and short plausible field values. No imagery budget needed.
why: The feature's idea, that the software reads your paperwork, is drawn in the image's contrast rather than stated by a caption or an icon.

name: cropped-product-film-off-the-page-edge
what_you_see: In a dark full-height section the left 38% holds a 22px statement and a four-row accordion with a dot on the open row. The right side holds a 1440x900 video placed at x=551, so about 550px of it runs off the viewport, and its edges are masked into the ground. The film shows a real pointer working through the app: opening a view, scrolling a list, hovering a row. The other rows' films wait paused at x=1991 in the same horizontal track, so changing row presumably slides the next one in (inferred from the layout; I did not click a row). The active clip started on arrival and read 1.01s, 2.42s, 3.93s while the others stayed at 0.
recipe: Sticky section 100vh, overflow: hidden, left column 551px. Flex track of videos, each 100vw by 100vh, object-fit: cover, translateX(551px) then minus 100vw per index, 600ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). Each video masked with a 10% top and bottom fade and linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #000 15%). Play only the active clip via IntersectionObserver at .5; on ended, advance. Record at 1440x900 at 2x, cursor visible, 8 to 11 seconds per topic, starting mid-task.
transfer: A bank records its real booking flow, a dentist the patient portal, a bakery the pre-order screen; crop so the film falls off the page edge.
depends_on: A real product or demo account and tidy screen captures.
why: It is an edited recording of someone using the thing, cropped hard by the viewport, so it reads as work in progress rather than a screenshot in a frame.

name: cursor-torch-on-a-privacy-promise
what_you_see: On pure black, a four-line centred paragraph at 64px/82px sits dim at 15% white in a 1095x328px block. A soft circle of full white about 400px across lights only the words under the pointer, cutting letters mid-word at its edge. I moved the pointer left and then right and the lit patch followed; with the pointer parked centrally the middle of each line is lit and the line ends fall away. The paragraph is about keeping data private, so you read it through a small pool of light. There is no image in the section at all.
recipe: Two stacked copies of the text, the top one aria-hidden. Base colour rgba(255,255,255,.15). Top colour #fff with mask-image: radial-gradient(circle 200px at var(--x) var(--y), #000 40%, transparent 100%). On pointermove set --x and --y in px, lerped by .12 in requestAnimationFrame; default 50% 50%. Font 64px/82px weight 600, letter-spacing .01em. On touch, drive --y with scroll position. The mask technique is inferred; the visible result was observed.
transfer: A bank uses it on a fraud promise, a clinic on its confidentiality statement, a bakery on an ingredient list. Once per site, on the sentence that matters most.
depends_on: One short paragraph worth reading slowly, a dark plain ground and a pointer.
why: The interaction is a metaphor for the sentence, a private torch on a private promise, built for this one paragraph.

name: headline-standing-in-a-rendered-nave
what_you_see: A dark CG hall of fluted glass columns recedes to a lit end wall at the frame's centre, filling 100% of the viewport as an 8.2s looping video. A white heavy serif at 114px on 100px leading stands on the same axis in two centred lines about 690px wide, with a sentence of about 20px below it landing just above the glowing wall. The columns rise on both sides and frame the words like a nave, so the wall reads as the room's only light source. Nothing is laid over the type; the image is the room and the heading is the thing standing in it.
recipe: Video full-bleed, 100vh, object-fit: cover, autoplay muted loop. Vanishing point at 50% across, 72% down. Headline centre at 45% height, font-size clamp(56px, 8vw, 114px), line-height .88, weight 700, tracking -0.004em. Edge vignette plus a bottom 20% fade to #000 so the next section begins black. Use tight leading so the two lines lock into one block.
transfer: A bank shoots its banking hall dead-centre at dusk, a clinic the corridor to the lit treatment room, a bakery the view down the racks to the lit oven.
depends_on: A symmetric one-point-perspective image with a lit centre and a heavy serif that survives over it. CG gives control; a real corridor also works.
why: The vanishing point and the headline were designed to share one axis, so the words appear to occupy the architecture rather than sit on top of a background.

name: story-first-blank-device-no-screenshots
what_you_see: For the first 2,000px there is no product: after the hero come a small tracked label and about 1.5 viewports of 70px serif text alone on black (size read from frames), whose words step from dim grey to white as they cross roughly 50 to 70% of the viewport height. When a phone finally rises out of the black at about 2,100px its screen is plain dark grey with one small logo and no interface. Balances, rates and charts do not appear; the first real product shots arrive in a tile rail at about 5,000px. Nearly every section is a heavy serif heading on pure black beside a single object. The effect is of a page that withholds, which suits a members-only pitch.
recipe: Order: hero, two viewports of text on #000, then one object with no interface on it. Word reveal: split words into spans, set opacity from .15 to 1 as each word's top crosses 60vh. Device: 320x640px rounded rectangle, #141414, 1px rgba(255,255,255,.12) rim, 56px centred logo, no screen content. Headline follows 120px after the object.
transfer: A private bank or an old family bakery tells the story first, shows one unlabelled object (a key, a loaf), and leaves rates and prices for later on the page.
depends_on: A real story that earns the reading, and a brand able to delay its proof.
why: Template logic shows the product early and often; this order sells status by refusing to, and that is a decision about sequence that no layout kit encodes.

name: door-of-light-as-the-last-call
what_you_see: The closing section is a render of a door ajar in a dark room, filling the left half of the screen: a blown-out white slit about 16% of the frame wide, with warm orange light falling across walls and floor. To its right sits heavy serif at 112px/108px in two lines, in a 690px box starting at x=750, and a small paragraph below. The light spills toward the type, so the heading seems lit by the door. I saw no animation in it across frames; it scrolls with the page.
recipe: Section 100vh on #000. Image at left 0, width 60vw, object-fit: cover, mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, #000 70%, transparent). Text at left 52vw, 112px/108px weight 700, tracking -0.005em, then an 18px/1.6 paragraph at 60% opacity, max-width 420px. Keep one warm hue against the black page; it should be the only warm area on the site.
transfer: A bakery's lit back door at 5am, a clinic's door half open, a bank's door at closing: end the page on a threshold instead of a coloured band.
depends_on: One lit-doorway image: a render or a real long exposure.
why: The final call to action is a picture of the offer itself, entry, rather than a banner with a button.

name: money-written-straight-onto-the-people
what_you_see: In a 571x571px rounded tile, a 7.5s video of two friends at a picnic writes a budget directly onto the scene. A white word appears beside the man, its amount appears across from it near the woman, then a second row and a third row arrive below it. No card, pill or panel sits behind the numbers; plain white text lies on clothes and grass. I sampled it at 0.9s intervals and saw one pair, then two, then three.
recipe: Square tile, outer corners 48px. Muted clip or photo as ground, linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 40%, rgba(0,0,0,.25)) over it. Three absolute rows at top 36%, 50%, 64%; labels left 12%, amounts right 12%; 26px/1 weight 500 white with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and text-shadow 0 1px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.35). Reveal rows 900ms apart, each 400ms opacity with an 8px rise. Bake it into the video if you need it robust. Row positions are estimates from small frames.
transfer: A bakery writes three ingredients and their farms over a photo of the baker; a dentist writes three treatment prices over a relaxed patient. Put the numbers on the picture with no card.
depends_on: A warm real-feeling photo with calm mid-tones, and three short values. Here it is a webm in the tile.
why: The figures are composited into a specific shot of specific people, so a budget reads as something happening inside a life rather than on a dashboard.

name: the-object-wears-the-rate
what_you_see: A glossy 3D pig in magenta and orange, about 290px wide, floats on black at the right of the section. The savings rate sits on its flank as a dark glass pill 160x90px with 40px text, overlapping its rear by about a third and hanging off it. The left column repeats the figure in a 64px heading. The rate is attached to an object in space rather than listed in a table.
recipe: Grid 1.2fr 1fr on a black ground. Cut-out render 290px wide with a soft colour bloom behind it (filter: blur(60px), opacity .35). Pill absolute, right -30px, bottom 18%; 160x90px; radius 999px; background linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(40,40,44,.9), rgba(14,70,60,.9)); 1px border rgba(255,255,255,.16); 40px/1 weight 600.
transfer: A bakery pins the price on the loaf, a dentist pins a monthly plan on a toothbrush. One number, one object.
depends_on: A simple cut-out object, either a 3D render or a clean product photo on transparency.
why: A single figure was given a physical host, so the most important number becomes a picture instead of a row.

name: money-chips-at-hand-height
what_you_see: On the right half of a rounded panel, a woman at a crossing holds a phone out at waist height and looks over her shoulder. Three stacked white chips, a 238x140px value card with a small line chart and two 70px-tall holdings pills, sit on her torso level with the phone, so the phone seems to be emitting them. Her face and the upper half of the frame stay clear. In a sister chapter two 194x66px pills sit exactly in the gap between a hand drawing a card from a bag and a hand holding a phone.
recipe: Image panel position: relative. Chip stack absolute, left 28%, top 42%, width 240px, gap 5px. Value card radius 28px; pills radius 36px; white at 95%; box-shadow 0 12px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18). Align the top of the stack to the hand. Never cover a face. Let the phone emerge from behind the stack by no more than 20px.
transfer: A dentist sets a next-visit chip beside a patient's hand; a bakery sets today's bake beside the baker's hands. Place the slip where the person is already looking or reaching.
depends_on: Photography of a person holding the phone or card, face turned away from the lens, with calm clothing at mid-body.
why: The chips are positioned for this one photograph, between the hands and below the gaze, so the interface and the person share a gesture.

name: photo-window-grows-into-the-room
what_you_see: On load a flat teal field carries a white headline and a small photo box, about 49% wide and 46% tall, at bottom centre. With no scroll, between about 2.4s and 2.9s, the photo grows to fill the whole viewport behind the headline, the teal goes, and the same words stand on dark treetops. The whole composition scales rather than cropping, since the small box shows the same framing as the large one. A cookie scrim was arriving at the same time, so I timed it from frames 500ms apart and could not read its easing.
recipe: Stage 100vh in the brand colour. Photo container absolute, inset 0, with transform: translate(0, 24%) scale(.49), radius 16px. After 2200ms animate to translate(0) scale(1), radius 0, over 700ms cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1). Headline above in z-order, unmoved. Pick a photo whose top band is dark enough for white type. Reduced motion: show the end state at once.
transfer: A bakery opens on a small framed loaf on its box colour, which grows into the shop. Two seconds of held composure, then one move.
depends_on: A photo that works at both sizes and carries the headline at full bleed.
why: The hero is staged in two states on a timer, a framed picture on a colour field that then becomes the room, which a static hero block cannot do.

name: product-list-set-as-a-paragraph
what_you_see: Where a template would place a grid of product cards, 17 product names run as one centred paragraph of 48px light serif, five lines deep, spanning about 82% of the width on white at 86px line spacing. Small square blue-grey points about 6px wide separate the names, with wide gaps either side. Three names carry a tiny black tag, 26px tall, set immediately after the word and holding the current rate or offer in 12px white sans. The block has no icons, no boxes and no headline of its own; the catalogue is the display type.
recipe: with text-align: center; font: 300 48px/86px serif; max-width 1200px; tight negative tracking (about -0.02em, estimated). Names as inline links. Separator ::after inline-block 6x6px #A9B4C2, margin 0 22px, vertical-align: middle. Tag inline-block, vertical-align: .2em, margin-left 8px, padding 7px 8px, radius 6px, background #000, colour #fff, 12px/12px sans. Keep rates in the tags so the paragraph stays a list of words.
transfer: A bakery sets all of today's bakes as one big paragraph with prices as tiny tags; a dentist lists treatments with 'from' prices; a bank lists accounts with rates, replacing the ruled rate table.
depends_on: A serif with real presence at light weight, and a catalogue of short names.
why: A CMS produces cards; this requires someone to set the catalogue as a single piece of type, deciding its line breaks and which words earn a live number.

name: unboxed-macro-behind-the-column-rules
what_you_see: On a black band, a very dark macro of a tilted device edge with two glass orbs occupies the upper right 45% with no frame. Its top is cut hard by a full-width hairline at the section edge, and its lower corner runs down to touch the 1px rules of three text columns. The heading sits left at half height, clear of the image. Below, three ruled columns of plain regulatory facts carry small dim regulator badges. Only tiny specular highlights are lit, so it feels like a serious object seen at low light rather than an illustration of security.
recipe: Section #000, padding 160px 80px 80px, position: relative, overflow: hidden. Image absolute, top 0, right 0, width 46vw, mix-blend-mode: screen so its blacks vanish, with a soft mask on the left edge. Three-column grid, gap 24px, each column border-top 1px rgba(255,255,255,.14), padding-top 28px. Regulator marks 28px tall at 70% opacity.
transfer: A safe's hinge, a dental mirror or a baker's blade shot on black, screen-blended so no box shows, above three plain columns of facts.
depends_on: A dark-ground macro photo or render with only specular highlights.
why: The image has no container and no padding; it is cut by the section's own rules, which is the opposite of a picture in a card beside text.

name: pinned-mess-then-one-calm-panel
what_you_see: Under a centred 40px heading, a wide collage fills about 85% of the width: a receipt photo, a stack of green spreadsheets, a policy document, forms, app icons and chat bubbles, all joined by thin curved lines. It holds in place from about 4,200px to 4,950px of scroll. At about 5,000px the heading swaps to its reply and within about 200px of scroll the whole collage fades to a ghost at about 10% opacity, while one white chat panel about 210x290px appears at centre. From 5,250px to 5,650px that panel fills with a request and ticking steps and a second panel appears beside it, over a faint grey wireframe of the same scene. It runs on two dotLottie files, one for the old way and one for the new; frames differ by scroll position but I did not separate scrubbing from timed playback.
recipe: Track calc(100vh + 1700px) with a sticky inner 100vh stage. Heading fixed at top of the stage, two text states crossfaded at 44% progress over 150px. Layer A: the collage, SVG or Lottie. At the same point animate layer A opacity 1 to .1 and filter: grayscale(1). Layer B: one 210px white panel, scale .96 to 1, with lines of text appearing as progress runs from .5 to 1. Keep layer A on screen as a ghost; it is what makes the calm legible.
transfer: A dentist piles up forms, reminder cards and phone notes, then fades them behind one booking card; a bank does it with a branch visit's paperwork.
depends_on: A truthful drawing of the old process with 10 to 15 real artefacts. No WebGL.
why: The argument is staged as a before and after in one spot, so the viewer watches clutter drain away, which needs a bespoke illustration of the customer's actual mess.

name: live-counters-as-a-ticker-strip
what_you_see: Below the hero stage runs a one-line strip of small pairs: an 11px uppercase grey label beside a 24px-tall pale pill with a running total. Digits roll vertically and I caught one mid-roll. The strip fades out at both ends and scrolls sideways under a fixed label on the left. Above the 64px headline, a tiny label carries a percentage to seven decimals, which I saw tick from 0.9734345% to 0.9734346% during load.
recipe: Row height 40px, flex, gap 24px, overflow hidden, mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #000 6%, #000 94%, transparent). Label 11px uppercase, tracking .02em, 50% ink. Value pill 24px tall, radius 6px, tabular numerals. Digit: span height 1em, overflow hidden, inner column of 0 to 9 with translateY(-n em), 500ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). Tick from real data or a truthful rate, and never invent a number.
transfer: A bakery counts loaves baked today, a clinic appointments kept this month, a bank the minutes people waited on hold. Small, honest and alive.
depends_on: A genuine count that changes, or a truthful daily total.
why: These are figures treated as instruments rather than stat tiles: small, in motion, and doubling as proof that the system is running now.

name: person-and-outcome-tile-in-the-grid
what_you_see: A hairline grid of 164px logo cells, six across, ends at right in a 327px-wide tile holding a portrait or scene. A small company tag and a 64px white outcome figure sit on the darkened foot of the photo. With no hover, the tile changed from one customer and figure to another within 5 seconds, and the logos around it were different between captures too. Small round arrow chips at cell corners mark the logos that have a story behind them.
recipe: Grid 164px cells with 1px hairlines and small plus marks at joints, right column 327px spanning two rows. Portrait object-fit: cover, gradient to rgba(0,0,0,.6) at the foot. Figure 64px/1 white, tag 13px. Cycle every 5s with a 400ms crossfade on photo and figure. Arrow chip 24px circle top-right of linked cells.
transfer: A dentist rotates a patient portrait with a plain result, a bank a shop owner with what the loan paid for, each with permission.
depends_on: Real customer portraits and one defensible number for each.
why: It breaks the logo wall with one human face and one measured result that keep changing, so the grid becomes a rotating case file rather than a row of marks.

name: one-bezel-free-window-for-the-whole-page
what_you_see: A rounded rectangle with no device frame starts about 433px wide in the hero, settles at about 326x705px (23% of the width, 78% of the height) and stays pinned at viewport centre through most of the page: to about 1,250px, then again from about 3,400px to 6,800px. A 40px heading to its left and a short paragraph to its right scroll past at page speed at staggered heights, while the page ground flips green, white, black, white, black. Inside the window, screens replace each other by sliding up within the mask: a hand holding a tag, a black panel with a 3D star, a ring chart, a full green number pad. It plays like one film in one window. The page scrolls in a nested 9,744px smooth-scroll container, the window contents are per-chapter mp4 and webm files, and there is no global GSAP, Lenis or THREE.
recipe: Column of chapters, each 150vh, with heading left and paragraph right. Stage position: sticky; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); width: min(23vw, 340px); aspect-ratio: 326/705; radius 50px; overflow: hidden; z-index: 2. No bezel. Each chapter owns one panel inside the stage; translateY from 100% to 0 tied to the last 30% of its chapter. Body background transitions on chapter change, 300ms. Clips all 9:16, same safe area.
transfer: A dentist keeps one tall window of the same patient through check-in, clean, X-ray and result; a bakery keeps one window of the same loaf from mixing to shelf.
depends_on: A set of matching vertical clips or screens, and copy short enough to pass either side.
why: The device is reduced to a mask and held still for the whole visit, so the page becomes a single continuous object rather than alternating left and right sections.

name: interface-breaks-apart-and-rebuilds
what_you_see: The hero is flat brand green with the window showing a balance. Stepping the real scroll position, by 100px the window has swapped to a card screen in pale tint, and by 300px the window and copy have dissolved into the green, leaving one white interface card low in the frame. White cards then stack back up, two at 400px, three at 500px, more at 600px, with the balance back at 700px and the screen's header at 800px. From 600px the green ground itself narrows from both sides as white comes in, until by about 900px only the window is left. So the interface is taken apart and reassembled while the brand colour collapses into the phone.
recipe: Build the screen as 5 to 6 absolutely placed cards in one stage on a full-bleed accent layer. Scrub 0 to 900px. 0 to 33%: stage opacity 1 to .1 except one card. 33 to 80%: cards return from translateY(24px), 100px of scroll apart, ending with the header. 66 to 100%: accent layer clip-path: inset(0 var(--c)) with --c from 0 to the width outside the window, so white arrives from both sides. Keep each card's final position identical to its first so they read as the same objects.
transfer: A clinic's appointment card or a bakery's order slip breaks into date, item and price, then rebuilds as the next message.
depends_on: A UI made of clear separate cards.
why: The transition uses the product's own components as the moving pieces, so nothing here could come from generic section fades.

name: window-rolls-up-and-the-card-drops-out
what_you_see: At about 1,100px the window starts losing height from the bottom. By 1,400px it is a strip about 190px tall at the top of the frame, and by 1,550px it is a 225x50px pill, while the ground has gone black. A portrait card rises from the bottom edge as the window closes, and by 1,550px it has turned to landscape, tilted about 20 degrees, on a fan of five coloured cards with its heading alongside. The phone appears to close up like a blind and hand you the physical object.
recipe: Stage height scrubbed from 100% to 8% across 450px with transform-origin: top. Card starts translateY(100vh) rotate(90deg), ends at 0 with rotate(-20deg) over the same scroll range, delayed by 100px. Fan: 5 cards absolute, rotate from -30 to 10 degrees, scale in from .9 with 40ms stagger. Background to #000 at the midpoint.
transfer: A clinic's screen closes and a printed appointment card fans out; a bakery's order screen rolls up and the box comes forward.
depends_on: A physical object that can be shot or rendered, plus the pinned stage above.
why: One element leaves and another takes over the same axis in one continuous gesture, a planned handoff rather than two sections with a gap.

name: four-tiles-four-media
what_you_see: Four 335x388px tiles with radii around 64px sit in a row, each 10px higher than the last, tops at 234, 224, 214 and 203px, like a gentle rising line; the stair may be scroll-driven. Each uses a different medium: a huge white number pill on flat green, a triple glyph built from black flip-dot blocks on white, a photographed still life, and a blurred green texture with a single notification card. The number showed three values across my frames, so the tile is a counting video, and each tile has a 20px pause button. Captions at 20px sit below and follow the stair.
recipe: Flex, gap 20px; tile aspect 335/388, radius 64px, overflow hidden; apply margin-top: calc(var(--i) * -10px) or a small per-tile parallax. Tile 1: flat accent with a white pill at 80% width, 80px numerals. Tile 2: glyph on a 12px block grid, CSS grid or SVG. Tile 3: studio still life, cover. Tile 4: a heavily blurred photo with one crisp card. Caption 20px/1.25 below. Add a visible pause for any motion over 5s.
transfer: A bakery: a big price, a stitched pattern, a photo of the box, a text from the shop saying it is ready.
depends_on: Four small assets in truly different media.
why: A card row normally repeats one recipe four times; here every tile is drawn in a different material while the frame stays fixed.

name: offer-printed-on-a-real-prop
what_you_see: One tile is a studio photo of a green tote bag on a yellow-green stool against a concrete wall, with pineapple leaves sticking out of the top. The offer's words are printed on the bag in white, slightly uneven with the fabric, and the domain appears on a small patch. There is no overlay type at all; the message exists as a physical object in the set. The bag's green matches the brand ground of the neighbouring tile.
recipe: Keep the image 1:1.15, cover, no overlay. Shoot on a neutral wall with one hard side light, prop in the accent colour, and one odd natural element for scale and wit. Text on the prop only, about 6% of the frame height.
transfer: A bakery prints the offer on a paper bag, a dentist on a toothbrush sleeve, a bank on a deposit envelope, and shoots it on a kitchen table.
depends_on: A physical prop and an hour with a camera. AI mock-ups risk looking fake here.
why: Someone printed the sentence on a thing and photographed it, which neither stock nor layout can do.

name: one-live-fragment-per-tile
what_you_see: Six pale tiles with 20px corners each hold exactly one piece of real interface, oversized and cropped. A dark action menu falls off the tile's right edge, a green status pill sits inside two soft concentric rings, a status timeline is cut by the top and right edges, a fee row fades out at left, and an emoji avatar rail is cut by both sides with its centre avatar larger. Short 16px titles and two grey lines of copy sit below. The fragment in each tile says one thing and nothing else. I saw these only as stills, so any motion in them is unverified.
recipe: Grid gap 34px; tile padding 0 for media, 24px for text, background #FAF9F7, radius 20px, overflow hidden. Media zone 200px tall. Render the real component at 1.4 times size. Deliberately let it exceed the zone on one or two sides; use mask-image at the fade side. Pill rings: box-shadow 0 0 0 8px and 0 0 0 16px in the accent at 15 and 8%.
transfer: A clinic shows a single appointment chip, a single reminder and a single price in separate tiles, cropped big.
depends_on: Real UI components you can render at larger scale.
why: Bento grids usually hold shrunken screenshots; these are single states chosen and enlarged until the tile's edge crops them.

name: catalogue-as-a-3d-stack
what_you_see: The home page is a full-viewport three.js canvas (r151) on a dark brown ground: each title is a 3D mesh with its printed jacket wrapped on spine and edges, and the books form one tower about 50% of the width. At 1.5s the tower is seen small with 13 spines tapering away; by 3s the view has closed in until four books fill the screen, 96 to 135px thick with 33 to 57px gaps. Scrolling descends the tower for about 3,500px with the spines seen in perspective. Hovering grew the book under the pointer by about 2%, and clicking a spine opens that book. The titles are readable only as printing on the objects.
recipe: Fixed canvas 100vw by 100vh, WebGL. BoxGeometry per book with six textures: spine, covers, page block. Camera x 0, y from scroll with damping 0.1, slight downward tilt. Book spacing 1.4 times thickness. On hover raycast and scale to 1.02. Spacer element 4000px tall to give the scroll. Keep an HTML list of titles for screen readers. Ground #231B1A.
transfer: A bakery stacks its loaves or cake tins, a bank stacks its passbooks through the decades, an archive its boxes. Works with any small set of objects.
depends_on: Scans of real products, WebGL, and an accessible fallback list.
why: The navigation is the inventory itself, a shelf you walk down, and no site builder has a pile of your actual objects as its menu.

name: medallion-turns-as-you-scroll
what_you_see: After the stack, a flat book cover in a starfield starts tilted at 3,700px and straightens to face you by 4,100px. Then the scene changes to a low-lit stone model city seen from above, with a red disc carrying printed words. As scroll runs from 4,400 to 5,300px the disc turns on its horizontal axis: a squashed ellipse, a full 350px circle at 4,700px, nearly edge-on at 5,000px with a small globe at its centre, then a ring behind the title at 5,300px. It loads a single glb model and the title passes through it. The white page rises over the scene like a curtain at the end.
recipe: In the same canvas, one glb disc with a texture per face. rotation.x = progress * Math.PI * 2 across 900px of scroll. Tilted plane version: rotation.x from 0.5rad to 0 across 400px. Directional light low from the left for long shadows. Final section position: relative; z-index above the canvas with a white ground.
transfer: A bank flips its old coin, a bakery its stamp, a clinic its seal as the page ends.
depends_on: A small 3D model and a canvas. CSS rotateX can fake a flat disc at no cost.
why: A small piece of the brand becomes a coin flipping in a built world, driven by scroll, as a reward for reaching the end of a page.

name: items-orbit-and-the-price-answers
what_you_see: A hand holds a phone rising from the lower centre of a dark hero, and five frosted tiles about 270px square, each with a cut-out product, ride a glowing violet arc that spans the full width. The tile at centre passes in front of the phone, larger and with a white label, while side tiles tilt up to about 25 degrees with faint tags. As each one arrives, the payment plan on the phone changes to suit that item; I read six different amounts across my frames. I checked the clock: it is a looping 9.17s video that keeps running at its own pace and does not follow scroll. The whole picture simply rises as you scroll on.
