recipe: Pre-rendered loop, 9s, 1440x810, placed at top 60vh with a fade at its foot. HTML alternative: tiles on a circle of radius 120vw, centre below the fold, rotate 72 degrees per step, 1.8s each. On step, update the phone's plan text with a rolling-digit change. Tile 270px, radius 40px, background rgba(255,255,255,.12), backdrop-filter: blur(16px). Label pill white on the active tile only. Arc: a 2px stroke with a 60px blurred copy in violet.
transfer: A bakery's cakes pass a counter display whose price changes; a dentist's treatments pass a monthly-cost card; a bank's goods pass a repayment figure.
depends_on: Cut-out product images and either motion software or a careful JS sequence.
why: Price is shown as a response to a real object, not as a rate list, and the phone is doing work inside the picture rather than posing on a gradient.

name: heading-holds-while-cards-deal-and-shrink
what_you_see: A one-line heading stays pinned 110px from the top under the nav while three 1320x600px panels scroll up and stick at 243px and 293px. As the next panel slides over, the one beneath shrinks: the first read scale .89 and then .86, the second .94. Their top edges remain visible above the newest card, as in a deck of cards. Each panel splits into copy at left and an image or interface at right.
recipe: Heading position: sticky; top: 110px. Cards position: sticky; top: 243px and 293px alternating; width 1320px; height 600px; radius 28px; transform-origin: top center. Scale = 1 - 0.14 * overlapProgress for the first, 1 - 0.06 for the second, driven by the next card's top relative to the viewport. No opacity change.
transfer: A bank's three accounts, a clinic's three plans or a bakery's three order sizes.
depends_on: Three items of equal weight and sticky positioning.
why: It keeps the context on screen and turns three repeated cards into one physical gesture, without any pinning library or a horizontal carousel.

name: wordmark-arc-plays-once-at-the-end
what_you_see: The last screen is a huge dim logotype about 1,250px wide in dark violet, set above the legal text. A glowing arc, the logo's own stroke, sweeps up over it and overshoots the top of the frame. It is a 1320x653px video that plays once over 5s, not on loop: it read 1.43s as it entered at 5,600px, 4.43s at 6,600px, and then stopped at 5.00s on its end frame. The page closes on a held image rather than a loop or a link grid.
recipe: Video 1320x653, no loop, no controls, muted, playsinline; play() when 20% is in view via IntersectionObserver. Hold the last frame. Legal text directly below in 12px at 55%. Use a 5s ease-out curve so it settles. Poster equals the final frame for reduced motion.
transfer: A bakery's stamp presses down once, a bank's crest draws once, at the very end of the page.
depends_on: A logo with one strong geometric gesture, and a short render.
why: The oversized wordmark footer is common, but here the mark's own geometry performs a single ending and then rests.

name: logos-as-pebbles-around-a-search-field
what_you_see: On a soft violet-to-teal panel 1320px wide, about 14 merchant logos appear as white circles from about 50 to 90px, scattered at irregular positions above and below a centred heading and a wide white search field. They look like pebbles around a pool. Sizes and distances vary with no grid. I saw no drift between frames, so it may be still in place.
recipe: Panel position: relative, height 780px, radius 28px. Logos absolute from a hand-placed list of 14 positions; widths 50 to 90px, white circle, box-shadow 0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.2). Heading and a 780x56px pill search field centred. Hand-place them: random scatter looks random.
transfer: A bank's accepted partners around a branch finder; a bakery's stockists around a postcode box.
depends_on: Round marks, and something to search or do at the centre.
why: The scattered logos are arranged around an action, the search box, so the wall of partners becomes an invitation to use it.

name: cursor-paints-the-other-self
what_you_see: The first screen has no headline at all: a cut-out head and shoulders stands dead centre on off-white, about 92% of viewport height and 55% of its width, with faint contour lines behind it and only a logo, a shop button and a 100px-wide info card in the corners. Moving the cursor across the face opens a liquid, irregular blob about 10 to 20% of viewport width that shows the same head, in the same position and scale, wearing the helmet. The blob trails the pointer and leaves soft contour-shaped smears on the background as well as on the subject. Text only arrives after the first scroll, so the first thing a visitor does is play with the subject.
recipe: Stack two same-size, same-registration images in a position:relative box. Draw the top one into a canvas: each frame, on an offscreen mask canvas, fade with fillStyle rgba(0,0,0,.06) under destination-out, then stamp a soft radial gradient of radius 110px at the eased pointer (lerp .14 per frame) plus two smaller stamps offset by a slow sine for an uneven edge. Then on the visible canvas drawImage(topImage), set globalCompositeOperation='destination-in', drawImage(mask). Result is the alternate image only where the cursor has been, healing over about 1.2s. On touch, run the stamp along a slow Lissajous path for 3s after load. Under prefers-reduced-motion, show a plain two-state toggle.
transfer: Two matched photos tell a story a sentence cannot: a dentist's smile before and after from a locked-off camera, a bakery's raw dough and baked loaf on the same board, a high street bank's branch in 1960 and today from the same pavement spot.
depends_on: Two images with identical framing and registration (a cut-out helps); canvas 2D is enough, the site uses a WebGL canvas (inferred from a full-viewport 1440x900 canvas).
why: It needs two images shot or retouched to register exactly, and the reveal is the content, so there is no slot in a template that it could fill.

name: hero-shrinks-into-a-card-and-gets-signed
what_you_see: As you scroll the first 840px, the full-viewport portrait contracts on its own centre: at 360px scrolled it is about 78% of the viewport each way, at 600px about 48%, and at 840px a 480x310px card (33% wide, 34% high) that has also lost colour to an olive-grey tint. The page around it has already gone from off-white to dark olive. Two lines of 106 to 110px type, one high-contrast serif in muted neon and one bold grotesque in off-white, run in opposite directions behind the card at its vertical middle, so the card cuts both lines. A neon handwritten stroke then draws itself over everything, starting as one slash at 600px and complete at about 1000px, spreading to 55% of viewport width and well past the card edges.
recipe: Section height 240vh, inner sticky 100vh, grid centred. Scrub progress p from section scroll. Image: animate width 100vw to 33vw and height 100vh to 34vh between p 0 and .45, object-fit:cover, and filter grayscale(0) to grayscale(1) plus an overlay multiply. Page background: interpolate on body from light to dark between p .05 and .25. Two marquee rows absolutely centred with z-index below the image, font-size clamp(64px,7.6vw,110px), line-height .9, translateX bound to scroll in opposite directions (row 1 -0.35px, row 2 +0.35px per scrolled px). Signature: inline SVG path with pathLength=1, stroke-width 16 at 1440, stroke-linecap round, stroke-dasharray 1, stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0 between p .3 and .7, z-index above image, width 55vw. Use CSS scroll-driven animation-timeline:view() where supported, with a small rAF fallback.
transfer: A founder's real signature, a head baker's handwritten note or a practice owner's name written across a small photo reads as a personal promise, and it costs one traced SVG. The shrink turns a big banner into a framed picture on the wall.
depends_on: A portrait or object that survives being small, one real hand-drawn SVG path, one saturated accent.
why: Hero, quote and marquee are one continuous object that keeps changing role under scrolling, so the sections cannot be separated into blocks.

name: cut-outs-face-off-across-the-headline
what_you_see: Two cut-outs bleed off opposite edges and face each other: on the left a helmet cropped by the viewport edge at about 23% of the width, on the right a head in profile at about 23%, each roughly 50 to 90% of viewport height. The gap between them, about 45% of the width, is the only place for type, which sits in two columns of two lines at 93 to 98px, line-height .82, serif above grotesque. The objects literally look at the words, and a neon scribble is hand-drawn across one word. Scrolling on, a full-bleed photo rises from the bottom with a hard straight edge and covers it all, and that photo holds both subjects together in one room.
recipe: Section 100vh, position:relative, overflow:hidden, background flat. Two absolutely positioned transparent PNG or WebP cut-outs: left:-6vw, width 30vw and right:-4vw, width 30vw, bottom aligned to the section. Text: centred block max-width 44vw, grid 1fr 1fr with gap 3vw, font-size clamp(56px,6.6vw,98px), line-height .82. Next section is a 100vw photo with margin-top:-100vh and sticky stacking so it slides over the pinned section: position:sticky; top:0 on the cut-out section, z-index 1 on the photo. Translate the photo inner image up by 12% over the rise for parallax.
transfer: Any pairing works: a loaf facing a bag of flour, a retainer facing a smile, a pair of keys facing a front door. Put the sentence in the gap and then cut to the real scene showing them together.
depends_on: Two clean cut-outs whose subjects point inward, and a follow-up photo that pays off the pairing.
why: The type column exists only because of the negative space between two specific silhouettes and their sight lines, so the layout is derived from the picture rather than a grid.

name: solid-bar-wipes-off-each-line
what_you_see: Every heading and paragraph arrives under solid bars. Each line is covered by a rectangle of exactly that line's height and text width, and the rectangle's left edge travels right, uncovering finished letters behind it. In the frame caught mid-reveal, a 93px heading has an 85px block left on its last word, ending exactly at the end of the word, while the paragraph below has three bars of 112, 366 and 205px, each stopping at its line's end. The bar colour follows the section: neon on olive and black, dark grey on off-white. Lines run at once but slightly offset, so a paragraph reads for a moment as a stack of bars of different lengths.
recipe: Split text into lines with a small splitter; each line display:block; width:fit-content; position:relative. Line ::after: position:absolute; inset:0; background:var(--accent); transform-origin:right; transform:scaleX(1). Add .in via IntersectionObserver at threshold .6 and transition transform to scaleX(0) over 640ms cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1). Stagger lines by 70ms. The bar's right end stays fixed on the line end while its left edge moves, which is what makes it read as a wipe. Set --accent per section. Re-split on resize, and show text plainly under prefers-reduced-motion or if JS fails.
transfer: A credit union or a clinic can use it in one brand colour on headings only, and it reads as someone highlighting the important line with a marker.
depends_on: Nothing more than a strong accent; must be reserved so it does not delay reading (under 700ms).
why: Templates fade text upward; here the entrance is a single colour-coded mechanical gesture that ties the whole site together.

name: section-edge-bows-then-flattens
what_you_see: A black section gives way to an off-white one, and the seam is not a straight line: the black section's lower edge bows downward across the full width, about 32px (roughly 4% of viewport height) deeper in the middle than at the left edge. Scrolling on, the bow relaxes and it is dead straight by the time the seam reaches the top of the screen, following scroll position, since all three frames were taken at rest. A tall photo straddles the seam, its top 20px above the curve, so the picture sits on both sections and hides the deepest part of the bow. Contour lines on the lighter section continue under it.
recipe: Upper section: position:relative; z-index:2; background black. Give it a pseudo-element at bottom: position:absolute; top:100%; left:0; width:100%; height:var(--bow); background:inherit; border-radius:0 0 50% 50% / 0 0 100% 100%. Scrub --bow from 40px to 0 as the seam travels from 100% to 0% of viewport height. The pseudo-element overlaps the next section, so no margin is needed. Put one tall image on the next section with margin-top:-20px and z-index:3 so it crosses the seam.
transfer: Works anywhere two sections change background: a bakery moving from a dark oven photo band to a cream menu section gets a soft, doughy seam for about ten lines of code.
depends_on: Two sections with very different grounds so the seam is visible.
why: A section seam in a template is a fixed straight or wavy divider; this one changes shape as the reader moves down, so the page has physical give.

name: catalogue-card-flips-to-object-in-use
what_you_see: A black wall of about 20 small cards in four columns, each about 23% of the width with a thin grey outline and one chamfered corner, staggered so neighbouring columns sit half a card out of step. Each holds a cut-out helmet at rest with a tiny name and year. Hovering replaces the cut-out with a full-colour photo of that same object in use, edge to edge in the card, and the outline turns neon. In one frame the hovered card also grows beyond its column, overlapping its neighbour and the edge of the wall. The grid is calm and monochrome at rest, so the single coloured card stands out.
recipe: Grid repeat(4,1fr), gap 16px; nth-child(even) margin-top:9vh for the stagger. Card: aspect-ratio 4/5, border 1px solid #2c2c2c, clip-path polygon with one 24px cut corner, position:relative. Two children: .specimen (cut-out, object-fit:contain, padding 12%) and .scene (object-fit:cover, inset 0, opacity 0, transform scale(1.08)). On hover or focus-visible: .scene opacity 1 and scale 1 over 380ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), .specimen opacity 0, border-colour accent, and on wide screens z-index 2 with transform scale(1.12) with transform-origin toward the grid centre. Keep the caption in the same place. On touch, first tap shows the scene.
transfer: A bakery's cakes as clean cut-outs that flip to the birthday table; a dentist's treatment list where each item flips to a real smile; a bank's account cards that flip to the thing that account paid for.
depends_on: A specimen shot plus an in-use shot for each item.
why: A hover usually lifts or zooms a card; here it changes the type of content from specimen to story, which needs a matched pair of assets per item.

name: sentence-parts-so-the-subject-falls-through
what_you_see: On a black pinned screen a figure stands centred at about 70% of viewport height, and three centred lines of uppercase text at about 88px (measured from a 98px line pitch) sit across it. Scrolling turns the figure around and it starts to fall away from the camera while the words move apart horizontally: first the gaps widen until the lines run past both viewport edges with a figure-width gap in the middle, cropping the outer words. The type then scales up hard, until one word is about 45% of viewport width and others are sliding off the top, as if the camera were passing through the sentence. The figure ends at about 8% of viewport height, alone in the dark, and the next scene opens around it.
recipe: Pinned section 400vh, sticky stage 100vh, perspective:800px, overflow:hidden. Wrap each word in an inline-block span with --dx set from its offset from the line centre (word centre minus stage centre, in px). Scrub p 0 to 1. Phase 1, p 0 to .5: each word translateX(calc(var(--dx) * var(--spread))) with --spread 0 to 1.2, keeping one central word on axis. Phase 2, p .5 to .85: translate3d the whole block with translateZ 0 to 700px so the words grow and pass the camera, opacity to 0 between .75 and .85. Subject is a transparent image or video behind the text with scale 1 to .12 over p .15 to .9 and transform-origin centre. Use font-size clamp(44px,6.1vw,88px), line-height 1.1. Under prefers-reduced-motion, show the sentence still.
transfer: No 3D needed. A bakery's line about one loaf can part around a cut-out loaf as it drops toward the table; a bank's sentence can open around a single key. Keep it to one use per page.
depends_on: One isolated subject on a plain ground and one short sentence, at most about 10 words.
why: The text layout is a function of scroll and of one subject's position, so the sentence is staged like an object in a scene instead of sitting in a text block.

name: screen-in-the-picture-becomes-the-page
what_you_see: A light section shows a heading and a dark tablet about 30% of viewport width, with a small figure visible inside its screen. Scrolling enlarges the tablet past the viewport: in one frame the rounded bezel corner is still visible at top right, tilted slightly, with the page's pale background showing beyond it and the figure now at about 60% of viewport height. A moment later the screen fills the frame and the whole page is black, so the next chapter is already happening inside the device. There is no cut, wipe or section seam.
recipe: Pinned wrapper 250vh, sticky 100vh. Device is an absolutely positioned box, width 30vw, border-radius 3vw, background black, with the next section's content inside it. Find the scale that makes the screen cover the viewport: S = max(innerWidth/screenW, innerHeight/screenH) * 1.05. Scrub transform scale 1 to S with transform-origin at the screen centre, translate that centre to the viewport centre, add rotateZ(-3deg to 0). Keep inner content counter-scaled until p .7 so it does not look enormous: inner scale = target/outerScale. Fade the surrounding heading out by p .3. On phones, keep the same effect with the device at 70vw.
transfer: A dentist's X-ray lightbox, a bank's phone app, a bakery's oven window: scroll up to it and go through it. Any shop window or doorway in a real photo can use the same trick with a clip-path hole instead of a device.
depends_on: A framed object in the first section (screen, window, door, ring); a dark or flat inner scene so the scale-up stays sharp.
why: The seam between two sections is removed by making the second section live inside an object in the first.

name: ribbon-threads-between-the-layers
what_you_see: A thick glossy tube, about 30px wide on a 1440 screen, enters from the page edge and travels with scrolling. In the intro section it arcs in a deep blue curve behind the 144px heading and wraps around a small image card, passing behind the card and showing again beneath it. In a later section it is cyan, running behind a three-line heading and down past a paragraph. It always sits between the page ground and the content, so it gives the flat layout physical depth, and it joins sections that would otherwise be unrelated.
recipe: Absolutely positioned SVG, full section width and height, z-index 0, with text and cards at z-index 1. One path hand-drawn over a screenshot of the finished layout, stroke-width 30, stroke-linecap round, fill none, pathLength=1. Scrub stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0 with the section's scroll, using animation-timeline:view() or a rAF scroll listener. To pass in front of one element, add a second clipped copy of the path at z-index 2 with a clip-path covering only that crossing. Depth comes from a subtle gradient across the stroke. Set vector-effect:non-scaling-stroke and redraw for phones, because the route will not match.
transfer: A dentist's patient journey or a bank's mortgage steps can follow one line through the page; a bakery can use a piped icing line or a ribbon of dough.
depends_on: A settled layout, since the path is hand-routed around it; one accent colour per section. The site's version is WebGL (inferred from full-page canvases), but flat SVG keeps the idea.
why: The line is routed around the specific layout of each section, so it can only be drawn once the content is placed.

name: media-card-bends-in-transit
what_you_see: A video card about 90% of the viewport width and 72% of its height sits between light sections. In one frame during scrolling the card stopped being a rectangle: the bottom edge bows upward and the lower-left corner is pulled about 25px inward, so the whole thing looks like a sheet of film under tension. In a repeat at the same scroll distance, at rest, it was a true rectangle with 20px corners, and it stayed flat for the next eight seconds. So the bend is transient; that it is driven by scroll speed is inferred, not measured. The content keeps playing throughout.
recipe: Read scroll velocity v each frame and smooth it with lerp .1, then clamp to -1 to 1 by dividing by 60px per frame. CSS-only version: wrapper perspective:1200px and inner transform rotateX(calc(var(--v)*5deg)) skewY(calc(var(--v)*.6deg)) with transform-origin centre top, spring back naturally as v decays. True edge bend: a WebGL plane with vertex y += sin(uv.x*PI)*v*.06*height, or an SVG feDisplacementMap with a horizontal gradient map and scale set to v*30. Limit to one element per viewport. Zero it under prefers-reduced-motion.
transfer: One large photo on any plain site (the shop front, the team) gains a little physical weight for about twenty lines of script, and nothing changes for anyone who is not scrolling.
depends_on: A smooth-scroll or velocity reading; the true curve needs WebGL or an SVG filter, the skew version needs nothing.
why: The shape appears to respond to the reader's movement, which no static layout or simple entrance animation can express.

name: control-sits-inside-the-sentence
what_you_see: Across the middle of the video card two words in very light type, about 105px judging by a 75px cap height, sit either side of a white pill 135x85px holding a play glyph, so the button reads as a word in the line. The whole group spans 50% of viewport width and is centred on the image. The clips behind change (three different ones in nine seconds at rest) while the words and pill hold still. A row of tiny + registration marks runs above and below the card at even spacing, like crop marks on a print sheet. The play control therefore needs no label of its own and no overlay darkening.
recipe: Flex row, align-items:center, gap .35em, font-size clamp(40px,7.3vw,105px), font-weight 300. Middle element is a button: width 1.5em, height .95em, border-radius 999px, background white, svg icon .25em. Hover: width grows to 1.9em over 300ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) so the words are pushed apart. Marks: a repeating grid of 9px + glyphs in a 1px-high row above and below the card, spaced at 25% of the card width.
transfer: Use it for any primary action: a bakery's 'Order [pill] today', a clinic's 'Book [pill] online'. It costs nothing and turns a button into a designed line.
depends_on: A short phrase that reads naturally around a control.
why: Play buttons normally float as an icon over media; here the control is typeset as a character in display type.

name: named-speech-box-replaces-the-explainer
what_you_see: After a hand-drawn envelope loader on white, the scene opens on a full-bleed illustrated roadside with a character standing centred, about 80% of viewport height, looking at the reader. Over her lower body sits a white speech panel about 50% of viewport width, slightly skewed so no edge is quite straight, with a blue tilted name tab attached to its top-left corner and small hand-lettered capitals inside. A blue square arrow button sits at the panel's bottom-right, which presumably advances it (inferred, not tested). The opening line of the piece is delivered this way, by someone, with no nav bar on screen. I saw only this first line, not what follows.
recipe: Fixed panel: left 50%, bottom 6vh, translateX(-50%), width min(52vw,720px), padding 28px 36px, background white, border 2px solid ink, clip-path polygon with corners nudged 1 to 2% so it looks cut by hand. Name tab: absolute, top -22px, left 12px, rotate(-2deg), accent ground, 15px caps. Text types on at 28ms per character; arrow button is keyboard focusable and Enter or Space advances. Clicking mid-type completes the line. Provide a skip control and render all lines in the DOM for screen readers.
transfer: A dentist's receptionist photographed once and given a name tab can walk a nervous patient through a first visit, one short line at a time, instead of a wall of FAQ text.
depends_on: A named character or real person with a distinct voice, and copy written as speech.
why: The interface belongs to the world of the piece, so information has a speaker and a voice instead of a heading and body copy.

name: scene-fogs-out-next-rises-from-it
what_you_see: Instead of a section boundary, the landscape dissolves into pale fog: the mountains and dome lose contrast, red and cyan fringes appear on their edges, and the frame goes almost flat grey-blue. While the old scene is still faintly visible near the top, the next object rises from the bottom edge inside the same fog. By the next stop only that object remains, floating in empty haze at about 55% of viewport height. Ground colour barely changes throughout, so the two scenes feel like one place.
recipe: Stage sticky 100vh, section 250vh. Layer A photo: filter blur(0 to 16px) and opacity 1 to 0 over p .1 to .55. Fog layer: full-size, background the page ground colour with a soft noise PNG, opacity 0 to .9 over p .05 to .45. Layer B cut-out: translateY(70vh to 0) over p .3 to .8, filter blur(10px to 0), under the fog until p .6 and fog then fades to .2. Chromatic fringe (optional): duplicate layer A twice with mix-blend-mode screen, tinted red and cyan, offset by ±calc(var(--p)*6px).
transfer: A bakery can go from the steamy kitchen to a single loaf inside actual steam; a spa or dentist can use a soft white wash to move between rooms without a hard section edge.
depends_on: Two subjects that share a tonal range; a cut-out for the incoming subject.
why: The transition is an atmospheric event with both scenes on screen together, where a template offers a fade or a hard cut.

name: specimen-tagged-with-leader-lines
what_you_see: A single rough crystal about 40% of viewport height floats at centre in empty grey haze, with something frozen inside it. Around it sit three small groups of 14px white mono text, a title top left, a reading top right and a date plus call to action bottom right, each joined to the object by a 1px line that ends on the crystal itself. Faint dotted grid points cover the whole frame. As you scroll, the object rises and turns and the labels travel with it, staying attached.
recipe: Stage relative, object centred. Labels absolutely positioned at offsets from the object box; SVG overlay with polyline elements from label underline to anchor points on the object, stroke white, 1px. Store anchors as percentages of the image box. On scroll, move object and labels with one shared transform so they stay together. Mono type 13 to 14px, uppercase, line-height 1.2. Lines draw on with stroke-dashoffset over 500ms, then the label text resolves. Group labels as a dl for screen readers.
transfer: A loaf labelled with hydration, proof time and crust temperature; a crown labelled with material and lifespan; a debit card labelled with its real fee numbers. Honest specifics become the decoration.
depends_on: One object with a strong silhouette on a clean ground, and real facts worth labelling.
why: The labels are positioned by the shape of one object and follow it, so the listing is treated as an annotated specimen rather than a card.

name: small-print-decodes-itself
what_you_see: The tiny 13 to 15px mono text in the corners does not fade in: it resolves character by character from wrong letters, so a mid-state frame shows a legal line reading as a garbled mix of real and random letters, and a sound label ends in a nonsense word. A frame moments later shows the correct text. Project titles and labels behave the same way, with wrong characters in the mid-state. The largest element on screen is untouched, so this is only a shimmer around the edges of the frame.
recipe: For each [data-decode] element, keep the final string. On reveal, run a timer every 30ms for about 600ms: characters before an advancing index show the true letter, the rest show a random pick from a charset of the same width. Requires a monospace font so width does not jitter. Set aria-label to the final string and aria-hidden on the animated node. Run once per element; skip under prefers-reduced-motion.
transfer: A bank's reference numbers, a clinic's opening hours or a bakery's batch number can resolve this way for a sense of a live system, using one small script.
depends_on: A monospace face. Use on labels only, never on body text.
why: Even the footer-grade copy has been given a behaviour, so the smallest type on the page feels alive.

name: line-drawing-resolves-into-the-room
what_you_see: At first paint the whole viewport is a white wireframe on black: a two-storey interior with stairs and a mezzanine, drawn in 1px lines, with small clusters of pixel blocks drifting in the air. Shortly after, the same camera view is a fully lit, dark 3D room with warm shelf lighting, a figure on the stairs, a dog, an arcade cabinet, a neon sign and a stack of old monitors. Line drawing and render share exact perspective, so the room seems to be built in front of you rather than loaded. I saw the two states about two seconds apart and cannot say whether a timer or the pointer triggers the change.
recipe: Without WebGL: trace the hero photo into an SVG line drawing in the same viewBox. Stack svg above img in one box. Show the SVG first with stroke-dashoffset drawing on over 900ms, then on img.decode() reveal the photo: mask-image linear-gradient sweep over 800ms or a simple opacity 0 to 1, with the lines fading to 0 after. The photo must not move or rescale when it appears. With a 3D scene, render wire material first and swap materials when textures finish.
transfer: An architect's or kitchen fitter's real plan drawing resolving into the finished photo; a bakery's pencil sketch of its shop front becoming the photograph.
depends_on: One strong interior or object image and a traced line version in identical perspective. The site uses three 1440x900 canvases, Geist and Geist Mono; no global GSAP or Lenis found.
why: The loading state is a designed drawing of the same picture, so waiting becomes the first scene instead of a spinner or skeleton.

name: objects-in-the-picture-are-the-menu
what_you_see: Pointing at the tall wall of shelves in the room fills that whole area with a fine diagonal hatch and a thin outline, following the perspective of the wall, and a small 13px label in square brackets appears at the cursor offering to go to the work section. The image takes the full viewport below a thin 36px nav. Nothing in the picture looks like a button until you move over it. The ordinary nav stays at the top, so this is a second, playful route rather than the only one.
recipe: Full-bleed img with an absolutely positioned SVG overlay in the same viewBox. One polygon per zone, traced by hand on the perspective of each object, fill transparent, wrapped in an a element. On hover or focus: fill url(#hatch) where the pattern is a 6x6 tile rotated 45deg with a 1px line at 35% white, stroke white at 1px, transition 150ms. Label: 13px mono in brackets, position:fixed, following the pointer with an 8px offset; show it at the zone centre on keyboard focus. Keep every link in a real nav as well, and give each polygon an aria-label. On touch, show the hatch briefly on load so people learn it is tappable.
transfer: A photo of a bakery counter where the bread shelf, the till and the oven each lead somewhere; a dentist's reception where the desk means booking and the door means treatments.
depends_on: One photo with several distinct objects. No 3D needed; hand-traced polygons only.
why: Navigation is mapped onto the geometry of a specific picture, so it can only exist for that image.

name: switch-the-whole-site-to-plain-text
what_you_see: A small black pill fixed at bottom centre holds two mono words, the active one in orange. Clicking the second word swaps the entire page for a 640px centred column of orange monospace text on black, topped by a logo built from pixel blocks, a row of slash-prefixed links and key-value rows joined by dot leaders. The page describes itself as a plain-text mirror for agents, crawlers and people who prefer it raw. The pill stays in the same place with the colours swapped, so getting back is obvious. The switch turns a 3D showpiece into a text file in one click.
recipe: Fixed pill: bottom 24px, left 50%, translateX(-50%), padding 8px 14px, 13px mono, two buttons with aria-pressed. Render the plain view as server HTML at its own URL so it works with no JS, and swap on click with a 200ms crossfade. Column max-width 640px, mono 14px, line-height 1.4. Rows: display:grid; grid-template-columns:14ch 1fr with dots written as characters. Remember the choice in try/catch-wrapped localStorage. Do not make people choose; the rich view is the default.
transfer: This suits plain businesses better than studios: a bank's 'just the rates', a bakery's 'just the menu and prices', a clinic's text view for screen readers, older patients and AI assistants.
depends_on: Content written so it stands alone as text, and a mono face.
why: The site has a second, fully designed personality with the same content, offered as a feature instead of hidden as a fallback.

name: archive-as-objects-on-a-shelf
what_you_see: The page does not scroll and has no headline. On a pale grey wall, two white shelves about 80% of viewport width each hold five square sleeves about 13.5% wide, leaning slightly back and casting long soft shadows downward. Each sleeve carries its own art, so ten releases read as a physical collection on sight. The only other text is a 14px two-line note at top left and, along the bottom edge, a ruled index of ten small columns giving year, season and name. The whole product history fits in one glance.
recipe: Without WebGL: stage 100vh, background linear-gradient on grey, perspective 1400px. Two grid rows of five, each item aspect-ratio 1, transform rotateX(4deg) with transform-origin bottom. Shelf: 8px white bar below each row with box-shadow 0 40px 60px -20px rgba(0,0,0,.25). Item shadow: a blurred dark skewed pseudo-element below the shelf. Foot index: flex row with 12px text, three lines each, each a link to the same item, and hovering it lifts the matching sleeve. Stack to two per row on phones and let it scroll.
transfer: A bakery's seasonal menus as printed cards on a rail, a building society's annual reports on a shelf, a clinic's patient guides in a leaflet rack.
depends_on: A set of 6 to 12 items with real cover art. The site uses one full-viewport canvas (WebGL inferred) and Inter; no GSAP or Lenis found.
why: A list of past items is shown as a place with lighting and gravity, instead of a grid of cards or a timeline.

name: chosen-item-steps-out-and-the-room-blurs
what_you_see: Hovering a sleeve lifts it off the shelf by about 4% of viewport height, swells it slightly and shows two small pills on its lower edge, while neighbours stay put. Clicking sends it to the centre of the screen at about 28% of viewport width and 46% of its height, and everything else on the wall goes soft with a strong blur. A 24px title and a one-sentence line appear at far left, level with the shelf, and one black pill sits under the sleeve. The sleeve also tilts a little toward the pointer. The URL stayed the same, and the shelf is still there behind it, so you never feel you have left.
recipe: Measure the item with getBoundingClientRect and use a FLIP transform to fly it to centre over 600ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), or use the View Transitions API with one view-transition-name. Background layer: filter blur(10px) over 400ms, scale 1.02 so edges do not show. Pointer tilt: rotateY((x-.5)*10deg) rotateX((.5-y)*8deg) with a lerp of .1. Close on Esc or a click outside, restoring focus to the item. Replace blur with an opacity drop under prefers-reduced-motion.
transfer: Any list of things: a cake from a shop's range, a mortgage product, a treatment. The item comes forward and the rest of the shop stays visible behind it.
depends_on: Items with good cover images; a blurred ground that stays recognisable.
why: The detail view is the same object moving through the same room, so there is no modal box, page change or dimmed overlay.

name: drag-the-cover-over-to-read-the-back
what_you_see: Dragging the centred sleeve turns it over like a record. The back carries the same art with noise dissolved through it, a left-aligned list of about nine contents lines in 18px, a small edition mark at lower left and a QR code at lower right, like real packaging. A small white pill reading Flip follows the pointer around the sleeve. Text and art are slightly tilted with the object, so the list reads as printed on it and not as an overlay.
recipe: Card: position:relative, transform-style:preserve-3d, transition none during drag. Faces: position:absolute, inset:0, backface-visibility:hidden; back has rotateY(180deg). Pointer drag: angle = start + dx*.5. On release, snap to the nearest multiple of 180 with a spring (cubic-bezier(.3,1.4,.5,1), 500ms). Plain click and Enter also flip. Label pill: position:fixed, follows pointer with lerp .2, hidden on touch. Make both faces real text, and aria-hidden the face that is turned away.
transfer: The back of the packet is where honest detail goes: a loaf's ingredients and allergens, an account's fees, a treatment's steps and price. Front sells, back informs.
depends_on: A square or card-shaped object with something real to print on its back.
why: The summary of contents lives on the back of an object you physically turn over, which makes reading a list feel like handling something.

name: product-moment-dissolves-into-the-page
what_you_see: Product shots are not screenshots in frames. A dark interface sits straight on the near-black page, and its far side and lower rows simply fade into the background, with no window edge. In the clearest example, a bright thread panel about 33% of viewport width sits forward at left, overlapping a kanban board that dims to almost nothing by the right edge, so the eye reads one exchange in the product and only senses the rest. The type inside is real-looking and legible, and a message is shown part-way through being typed. It looks like one specific moment of use, not a tour of the interface.
recipe: Build the UI crop in HTML or use a real capture at 2x. Wrapper position:relative; overflow:hidden. Apply mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg,#000 45%,transparent 95%), linear-gradient(180deg,#000 60%,transparent); mask-composite:intersect. Foreground panel: absolutely placed, overlapping by 12% of its width, background slightly lighter than the page, 1px border at 8% white, box-shadow 0 30px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.5). Write realistic content that tells one small story. Whole thing width 100% of the content column, bleeding past the fold.
transfer: A bank shows one notification and the balance it changed, with the app fading out. A clinic shows one booking confirmation. One real moment beats a full-screen mock-up.
depends_on: Software or a form worth showing, a dark or plain ground matching the UI. No canvas, GSAP or Lenis found; Inter Variable and Berkeley Mono.
why: The picture is edited down to a single story beat, which needs someone to decide what to hide, while template mock-ups show a whole screen in a frame.

name: benefits-as-numbered-figure-plates
what_you_see: Where a template would put three icon cards, there are three tall columns split only by faint hairlines, with no card backgrounds. Each carries a tiny mono label at the top like a figure number in a technical manual, then a 1px isometric line drawing about 20% of viewport width, then a short title and two lines of grey text at the very bottom. The drawings are abstract, stacked plates, blocks and steps, all in the same line weight and angle. Above them runs a single 44px or so sentence, white for its first phrase and grey for the rest. Hovering the drawings did nothing in my test.
recipe: Grid repeat(3,1fr), each column border-left 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.07), padding 24px, min-height 56vh, flex column with justify-content:space-between. Label: 11px mono uppercase at 35% white. Drawing: SVG, 1px stroke at 45% white, one isometric angle throughout, 30 degrees. Sentence above: font-size clamp(28px,3vw,44px), line-height 1.1, letter-spacing -.02em; second span colour at 55% white.
transfer: A solicitor or dentist can number their three promises as Fig. 1 to 3 with simple line drawings of a key, a tooth and a clock, and instantly look more careful than an icon set.
depends_on: Three simple line drawings made to one rule; a mono face for labels.
why: It takes the common three-up and rewrites it in the language of an engineering manual, with one commissioned drawing system in place of stock icons.

name: film-recedes-into-a-wall-of-work
what_you_see: A black card holding a product film rises under a short statement and reaches about 92% of viewport width, then keeps shrinking as you scroll: about 75% at the next stop, then 58%, then 38%. As it shrinks it turns out to be one tile of a larger wall: neighbouring dark tiles slide in around it with 16px gaps and 8px corners, each holding a different product on black. Scrolling on, the wall moves while the sentence holds its place. No section seam occurs anywhere in this run; one film becomes the whole portfolio.
recipe: Pinned section 300vh, sticky 100vh, overflow:hidden. Build the wall as a CSS grid 3 columns wide, sized at 270vw so the centre tile fills the viewport at scale 1. Scrub transform scale 1 to .37 on the grid about the centre tile between p .1 and .6, so neighbours arrive naturally without separate animation. Then translateY each column by a different amount (-10vh, -24vh, -6vh) between p .6 and 1. Use muted, inline, looping video in each tile, poster images, and pause tiles out of view with IntersectionObserver.
transfer: A wedding baker's one cake film pulling back into a wall of twelve cakes; a builder's one kitchen becoming the full set of projects.
depends_on: Six to nine pieces of matching tone on the same ground colour. The site does this with Lenis and 22 video elements, no canvas, so no WebGL is required.
why: The grid of work is arrived at by pulling the camera back from one piece, so the layout is the end of a shot rather than a block placed on a page.

name: statement-laid-across-a-blank-screen
what_you_see: In the centre tile stands a phone 270px wide and 580px high with a completely black screen, and a three-line white 42px centred sentence runs straight across it. The text is about 450px wide, so it overhangs the phone on both sides by about 90px, and the phone's bright edges pass behind the words. The blank screen gives the sentence a quiet ground while the surrounding tiles keep showing colourful product. The device looks momentarily switched off so it can say something.
recipe: Tile position:relative; display:grid; place-items:center. Device image centred at height 64vh with a pure black screen. Text absolutely centred over it: width 31vw, font-size clamp(26px,2.9vw,42px), line-height 1.1, letter-spacing -.02em, text-align center, z-index 2. Text must overhang the device by at least 15% each side, or it reads as a screen UI instead of a statement.
transfer: A blank shop chalkboard, an empty window or a dark oven door photographed once becomes the place the headline sits, slightly wider than the object itself.
depends_on: A device, sign or frame shot with a blank dark area.
why: The device mock-up normally carries a screenshot; here it is deliberately empty and acts as the frame for the page's message.

name: words-pull-focus-one-at-a-time
what_you_see: Sentences do not fade or slide. Words sharpen from heavy blur like a lens racking focus, left to right: in one frame the first two lines are crisp while on the last line the words get progressively softer until the final word is a smear. Further down the scroll the same sentence goes out of focus as a whole while the wall continues behind it. The next sentence then arrives the same way, with its opening words sharp and the tail still soft and grey. Scrolling drives it, so the reader sets the pace of the reading.
recipe: Wrap each word in an inline-block span with --i index. Scrub p across the sentence's pin. Per word: local = clamp((p*(n+6) - i)/6, 0, 1); filter: blur(calc((1 - local)*14px)); opacity: calc(.15 + local*.85). Add will-change:filter only while pinned, and keep to one sentence on screen as blur is costly. Exit: blur the whole block to 10px over the last 15% of the pin. Show plain text under prefers-reduced-motion.
transfer: A hospice, charity or small bank's single key sentence coming into focus at reading speed gives a calm, considered tone with no imagery at all.
depends_on: Dark or plain ground; a short sentence; used once or twice a page.
why: The entrance imitates a camera instead of a slide-up, matching a site built almost entirely from film.

name: unseen-hand-edits-the-curve
what_you_see: Behind a heading, the whole viewport is filled by a single thick grey vector outline, about 12px wide on near-black, far too large to see its full shape. A blue anchor point with two handles on thin blue lines sits on the curve, and a large arrow cursor that is not the visitor's is dragging it. With no input from me the curve changed across frames 1.2 seconds apart, with the anchor and cursor in new places each time. It looks exactly like a designer working live in a drawing tool, at a huge scale. The heading sat blurred at lower left while this ran.
recipe: One SVG path sized to 140vw so it overflows, stroke 12px at #3c4650, fill none. Define 6 keyed paths with the same number of points, and interpolate point arrays over 1.6s with ease-in-out, holding .8s on each. On top: circle r 10 fill blue stroke white at the active anchor, two circles r 7 at its control points, 1.5px blue lines between. Fake cursor: an SVG arrow 56px tall pinned to the active anchor, offset 8px. Pause when off-screen and under prefers-reduced-motion, showing one static frame.
transfer: A sign painter's letterform, a bakery's logo being adjusted, a budget line a bank's cursor drags upward, a dentist's smile line being redrawn on a plan. Show the work happening.
depends_on: A meaningful outline, such as a logo or letter. SVG only.
why: It shows the act of making instead of the finished output, and it is built from an interface everyone recognises rather than a stock animation.

name: footer-sheet-turns-opaque-over-the-reel
what_you_see: The last section is a full-bleed film. As the page ends, a footer panel rises over it and starts out translucent grey, with the film visible through it, then turns solid white within a few hundred pixels of scrolling. It stops at about 60% of the viewport, so the film keeps running in a band across the top. At rest, that band kept changing, showing three different clips over nine seconds, one with a red colour wash. The footer is thus a calm white page held under a live picture, with a two-line 42px invitation.
recipe: Sticky reel: position:sticky; top:0; height:100vh; z-index:0. Footer: position:relative; z-index:1; margin-top:-60vh; height:60vh. Scrub background from rgba(255,255,255,.2) to #fff over the footer's first 25% of travel, using animation-timeline:view() or a scroll listener. Reel: 3 clips, crossfade every 3 to 4s. Keep footer text hidden until the panel is 80% opaque, so contrast never fails.
transfer: A bakery's oven or shop-floor loop running above its opening hours; a clinic's calm reception shot above its address.
depends_on: Several short clips of the same mood; one pinned layer.
why: The footer is a sheet sliding over a running film rather than a final block of links, so the page ends in a live scene.

name: crooked-window-opens-around-a-still-image
what_you_see: On a pale lilac page sits a dark four-sided window about 29% of viewport width and 72% of its height, in which no two sides are parallel: its top edge slopes down to the right and its right side leans outward. It looks like a card tilted in space, and an orb and the fingertips of a raised hand are cropped by it. As you scroll, the corners travel outward and the sides straighten: 55% wide, then 75%, then 85% with nearly vertical sides. The orb and hand inside hold their position and size, revealing more of the picture, so the window opens rather than the image zooming.
recipe: Pinned section 300vh; image sticky at 100vh, full-bleed, object-fit:cover, never transformed. Scrub clip-path between two four-point polygons with the same point order: start polygon(36% 8%, 60% 17%, 65% 73%, 36.5% 80%), end polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%). CSS animates this directly with animation-timeline:scroll(), or use a rAF lerp. Hold the start shape for the first 15% of the pin. Caption sits under the shape in 14 to 16px, fading out by p .3. For the 8px soft corners, use an SVG clipPath with rounded joins or the CSS shape() function.
transfer: A bakery's oven door shape opening onto the whole kitchen; a door ajar in a bank's branch photo opening to the full room. One image, no video needed.
depends_on: A full-bleed image that still works as a narrow crop in the middle. The site has ScrollTrigger and Lenis loaded, plus two 1440x900 canvases.
why: The motion is in the frame's corners and not the picture, and a template's image block can only scale or fade.

name: two-words-in-opposite-corners-object-between
what_you_see: The hero splits a two-word phrase across the diagonal of the screen. One word in heavy condensed 180px capitals sits top left, the other bottom right, and a glowing 3D object about 50% of viewport width fills the space between. The object overlaps the end of the first word and rises over the nav zone. A small 14px mono paragraph sits under the first word and runs into the object. You read the phrase by travelling across the subject.
recipe: Stage 100vh, black, position:relative. Word A: absolute, top 7vh, left 1.5vw. Word B: absolute, bottom 3vh, right 2vw. Both font-size clamp(72px,12.5vw,180px), line-height .82, weight 900, condensed. Subject: centred at 52vw, z-index above word A and below word B, shifted about 6vw right of centre. Paragraph: absolute under word A, max-width 26ch, 14px mono. Mobile: keep the diagonal with type at 22vw.
transfer: 'Fresh' top left and 'daily' bottom right with one loaf crossing between; 'Healthy' and 'smiles' around one apple. A plain photo cut-out does the work of 3D.
depends_on: A cut-out or object on plain ground with a clear diagonal, and a two-word idea. A heavy condensed face helps.
why: The headline is broken up and placed by the shape of the subject, so it cannot be poured into a text block beside an image.

name: numerals-straighten-under-the-pointer
what_you_see: Stats sit in an uneven collage of black, white and violet cards on a black page, in very heavy condensed figures up to 162px. Some figures rest warped: in one, the first numeral is about twice the size of the last character, the baseline tilts and letters shrink along the row as if seen in a bent mirror. I tested this at rest: with the pointer on that card the same figures snap to a flat, even line, and when the pointer leaves they warp again. The warped state held unchanged for nine seconds with no scrolling. It makes dry numbers something you want to touch.
recipe: Split a figure into spans. Rest state: each span gets its own scale and rotate, descending across the row (scale 1.6, 1.25, 1, .8, .62, .5), with transform-origin left bottom, plus rotate(-7deg) on the row. Hover or focus: all to scale(1) rotate(0) over 450ms with cubic-bezier(.2,1.3,.4,1). Keep the real number in aria-label on the parent and aria-hidden the spans. On touch, flatten when the card scrolls to the centre. Check that the warped state stays legible. Card sizes: mix at least three heights and offset columns by 8 to 15vh.
transfer: A bank's savings rate, a bakery's '3 am start', a clinic's waiting time: one playful number that sits up straight when you point at it. Use it on a single card, not a whole table.
depends_on: A heavy condensed face and at most three or four numbers that matter.
why: Stats normally count up once on entry; here each figure has a resting pose and responds to the visitor, and the resting pose is the distorted one.

name: picture-bursts-out-of-the-headline
what_you_see: A seven-line centred headline in 90px heavy condensed capitals, about 45% of viewport width, has tiny dark squares set in word gaps on three lines, each about the size of a full stop made huge. With the pointer in the middle of the headline, a colourful picture about 18% of viewport width and 23% of its height appears on top of the type, covering parts of two lines. Moving on, the headline is clean again. I saw the image appear with the pointer over the headline, but could not establish whether the squares themselves trigger it.
recipe: Headline: text-align center, font-size clamp(44px,6.3vw,90px), line-height .86. Insert inline-block tokens .35em square, background ink, vertical-align .15em, between chosen words. Each token owns a hidden img: position:absolute, width 18vw, aspect-ratio 5/4, transform scale(.1), opacity 0, transform-origin at the token. On token hover or focus: scale 1, opacity 1 over 240ms with cubic-bezier(.2,1.4,.4,1). Give tokens tabindex=0 and an aria-label. On touch, open each once as the line reaches the middle of the screen.
transfer: A bakery's sentence about sourdough, rye and seeded loaves where a dot after each word pops open a photo of it. It works in any text-only section with no layout change.
depends_on: A statement with several concrete nouns worth illustrating.
why: Images are hidden inside a sentence and appear in the middle of reading, so the pure type block has a surprise in it.

name: address-set-as-a-typographic-composition
what_you_see: The footer's contact details fill the bottom third of the screen in three lines of a condensed high-contrast serif at about 90px, justified by eye so the lines run about 70% of viewport width. Between the words sit custom ornaments the same height as the type: a diamond holding a letter, map coordinates stacked in two bold 22px rows between small arrows, a quatrefoil, boxed and ringed letters, a curved double arrow, a phone number built as a ruled fraction-like table, and a long looping swash standing in for the at sign. Every piece of plain data has become a small drawing. A boring address is the best-looking thing on the page.
recipe: Set three lines at font-size clamp(40px,6.2vw,90px), line-height 1.1, in a condensed serif. Inline ornaments as SVGs with height 1em and vertical-align -.12em, or as ligatures in a small custom font. Stacked coordinates: inline-grid of two rows at .24em bold, between tiny arrow glyphs. Phone: inline-grid with 1px borders, area code in one cell and the two number groups stacked in the next. Keep the real text available: wrap the block in an address element, aria-hidden the ornaments, and keep tel: and mailto: links on the real values. Break by hand at each width.
transfer: This is the most directly useful move for a local business. A bakery's address, hours and phone number, drawn into one big composition with a wheat ear and a clock, becomes the poster for the shop.
depends_on: A distinctive display serif; 6 to 8 small drawn ornaments; custom font LocomotiveNew plus Helvetica Now on the site, with Lenis and two small canvases.
why: The most neglected text on a site is hand-composed, with ornaments drawn for this exact string.

name: list-row-grows-its-own-thumbnail
what_you_see: The work index is a stack of centred names in a 110px condensed serif, each in a 150px row between thin black rules running the whole content width. With the pointer on a row, a small image about 167x114px appears inline straight after the name, at the same height as the letters, and the name shifts left to keep the pair centred. It works on the row under a still pointer while scrolling too, so names light up as they pass under it. There is no floating preview chasing the cursor and no card, just a picture joining the sentence.
recipe: Each row: a link, display:flex; justify-content:center; align-items:center; border-bottom:1px solid currentColor; height 150px; font-size clamp(44px,7.6vw,110px). Thumb: inline img with width 0, height .95em, object-fit:cover, margin-left 0; on hover or focus width 1.5em, margin-left .15em, transition 380ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). Animating width makes the centred name slide by itself. Lazy-load thumbs. Touch: show the thumb on the row nearest the centre of the screen.
transfer: A dentist's treatment list, a cafe's menu or a bank's branch list set big with a tiny photo joining each name. It turns a plain list into the main feature for almost no work.
depends_on: One small image per row and short names. A big condensed face keeps long names on one line.
why: The image takes a place in the line of type, so text and picture share one baseline, instead of an image appearing in a separate hover layer.

name: caption-broken-around-the-picture
what_you_see: A small black image card about 31% of viewport width sits on a white page, off-centre, and its 15px caption is broken into three pieces placed around it: the first words sit above its left edge, the next ones to the left of it at mid-height, and a date range to the right. Another card further down has a two-line caption whose second line is indented by about 8% of the width. The small text is scattered deliberately, so the image seems to hold the words in orbit. On a very restrained black and white page, that is enough to feel designed.
recipe: Grid 12 columns. Image spans columns 5 to 8. Caption pieces are separate spans placed in the grid: piece 1 at column 4 to 5, aligned to the image's top with translateY(-1.4em); piece 2 at column 3 to 4, align-self:center, text-align:right; piece 3 at column 9, align-self:center. Size 15px, line-height 1.3. On phones, gather them into one line under the image. Read aloud order must still make sense in the DOM.
transfer: 'Baked / since / 1962' around one photo of the first shop; 'Open / until / six' around a door. No new assets, only a decision about where words go.
depends_on: A phrase that can be split, and generous white space.
why: Captions are composed in space around one image rather than sitting in a line beneath it, and each placement is set by hand.

name: name-rail-repaints-the-whole-screen
what_you_see: The home page is one screen that does not scroll. A rail of ten small glass pills sits at the left, vertically centred, 38px apart in 16px type. Hovering a pill replaces the entire viewport within about a second with that client's own composition: one a huge olive arch with a phone card at lower right, one a figure made of paint with a monitor at upper right, one a full-bleed skin photograph with a phone card at left, one two colour fields split by a giant curve with an oversized smile mark. Each has a name in an 88px light serif and short lines in a different position, and the rail and header stay fixed. Leaving the rail returns to the default screen, and clicking opens the case study.
recipe: Stage fixed inset:0. Rail: position:absolute; left:24px; top:50%; translateY(-50%); flex column; gap 6px; pills with padding 4px 16px, background rgba(255,255,255,.14), backdrop-filter blur(10px), border-radius 999px. One section per item, absolutely stacked, opacity 0, each with its own hand-placed children. On pill hover or focus: active panel opacity 1 over 450ms, children translateY(16px to 0) staggered by 50ms. Preload panel images on first pointer movement. Pills are real links. On touch, stack the panels as a normal scrolling list.
transfer: A bakery's rail of cakes, breads and pastries, each repainting the screen in its own colour and photo; a small practice's five services, each with its own poster. Fewer items make it easier.
depends_on: Bespoke layout and images per entry, about 6 to 10 of them. Lenis and 3 videos on the site, no canvas; PP Eiko at weight 240 and Basis Grotesque.
why: Every entry has its own art-directed layout at full size, so the list of work is ten posters instead of ten rows or cards.

name: corner-clock-walks-through-the-cities
what_you_see: In the top right corner, a tiny 12px label shows a three-letter place code and that place's local time, and it keeps changing by itself: across my frames it showed codes such as LDN, CDG, TST, YYJ, NYC, SFO and FRA, each with a different time. It sits beside a small round contact icon and is easy to miss. It gives a static single-screen page a faint pulse and quietly says the company works around the world, without a word of marketing copy.
recipe: A list of { code, timeZone } pairs. Every 2500ms take the next pair and format with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', { hour:'numeric', minute:'2-digit', timeZone }). Swap with a 240ms vertical roll inside an overflow:hidden line, height 1.2em. 12px, tabular-nums. Add aria-hidden and keep a real list of locations elsewhere. Stop the rolling under prefers-reduced-motion and show one value.
transfer: 'Ovens on since 4:12', 'Open now, closes 6', 'Next appointment Tuesday 9:30', 'Phone lines staffed'. Real status from the business, in tiny type, says someone is home.
depends_on: A genuine live fact. Only a few lines of JS.
why: A fact about the business is delivered as a small live instrument rather than an 'our offices' section.

name: bar-behind-row
what_you_see: Ranked list where each label sits on a tinted bar scaled to its value: 36px pitch, 32px bar, radius 4, 10% tint, value right aligned at 14/500 in its own column. Bars stop short of the values. One tint per panel.

name: direct-label-chips
what_you_see: Lines labelled on the plot, no legend: filled 12/600 chips on 1px vertical leaders into each curve, single pale axes, 11px caps axis titles. Highlight series dashed in accent with an open-ring terminus and a bordered note. State when schematic.

name: bump-chart
what_you_see: Rank over time: smooth curves across 5 to 6 named columns, one highlighted in ink and the rest pale, rank labels at left, category pills above. Curves are safe here because only order matters. Say rank, not value.

name: aura-rim
what_you_see: Page-colour disc about 90% of viewport width, hard edge with 18px soft spread. Outside it a conic gradient of three warm hues peaks at the rim and falls to page colour by the corners. Centre the falloff on the disc. Use once.

name: horizon-from-the-base
what_you_see: Separate blurred ellipses, 44px blur, rise from the bottom edge to different heights, 150 to 540px, in four to six hues, with a near-white core at the very base. Fades to the dark page by mid-height. Grain sigma 3. Once, as payoff.

name: sawtooth-slats-and-blinds
what_you_see: Repeating ramps that end in a hard cut: 130 to 420px vertical slats, or 10px blinds, or 8px barcode strokes. Amplitude 12 to 25 levels, faded at both ends by a mask. The ramp gives light, the cut gives material.

name: page-long-hue-journey
what_you_see: One page-tall vertical gradient, 4 to 8 stops, hue shifting per section. Sections have no edges. Cards sit on it as glass or white. Keep stops in one value range so text colour never flips. Chapters are marked by colour, like time of day.

name: one-gradient-tile
what_you_see: Flat neutral page, with colour reserved for one tile or one family of tiles: a grain mesh of two opposed hues, sigma 5 to 10 levels, white type, radius 16 to 30px. Reuse it once, enlarged. It becomes the only hue on the page.

name: lit-edge-horizon
what_you_see: One very large curved edge, 1px, lit from behind: a rim running through a spectrum, or a section lid brightening across its central 400px. Soft pool below 8% white, falling off within 100px. On black. Once per page.

name: hard-cut-inner-bloom
what_you_see: A large black shape with a hard silhouette masks an accent fill. Inside the shape, the accent blooms about 120px into the black. Hard outer edge plus soft inner light reads as a cut-out lit from behind.

name: light-inside-the-render
what_you_see: All light belongs to the render: additive streaks, signs, rim fringes, soft shadow edges. No CSS glow over it. Background stays black or a flat floor. Bloom stays inside the image and falls to ground before its edge.

name: pixel-dissolve-edge
what_you_see: A block edge breaks into 14px hard squares over 200 to 360px. Odds fall on a curve with a long tail, neighbours raise odds, so mass dissolves. No blur. A section boundary becomes the signature graphic.

name: glyph-halftone-figure
what_you_see: Monospace glyphs or square dots on a 6 to 7px cell, density modelling a lit form about 550px, bleeding off one edge on a flat ground. Take tone from a render or photo, not a flat silhouette. Reuse small as icons.

name: enlarged-brand-geometry
what_you_see: Logo geometry enlarged to 200 to 800px, drawn one tone from its ground, 3 to 5 L* apart, sweeping behind sections with its own corners. Replaces a generic gradient on dark pages and CTA bands.

name: one-bit-dither
what_you_see: Reduce one photograph to pure black and white dots with no greys, applied to masthead, cards and slices alike. Crop or glitch it on load. One treatment only.

name: smeared-plate
what_you_see: Rotate a photo 8 to 14 degrees, directional blur 70px along x and 2 to 3px across, boost saturation, add grain .09. Flat plates behind every demo and logo, radius 8 or square, hue varying per plate.

name: graded-scene
what_you_see: One image or drawing graded to the page colour, with uniform value behind the headline. Line art sits one step above the wash, and grain ties it together. Black or white type needs no scrim because the sky is even.

name: lit-from-within-on-black
what_you_see: Tile is pure #000 with no CSS gradient. All light comes from the image, whose glow falls to black before its edges, so no rectangle shows. Export images on true black.

name: textural-photo-band
what_you_see: A material, sky or aerial photo, such as water, painted concrete or a dawn sky, used as a flat colour band 360px or taller with a title and CTA. Texture without a gradient, and no subject to compete with.

name: defocused-crushed-photo
what_you_see: Full-bleed photo heavily blurred and graded to a near-black hue, about 10% visible detail, with grain. Reads as texture until you look. A sharp device or table sits on top with no scrim.

name: photo-dissolve-seam
what_you_see: The page dissolves over its last 400px into a low-contrast cloud or fog photo, or a dark page lifts into fog and back, masked so no image edge shows. A panel or CTA floats in the air.

name: no-caption-tile
what_you_see: Flat 3:4 tile in #f2f2f2 or one tone off the page, radius 0, no name, price or badge at rest. Cut-outs alternate with tight detail crops. 10-12px gaps, 12px caps label above the rail, partial tiles at both ends. Use only for a campaign rail that leads to real listings.

name: bare-product-no-card
what_you_see: No tile or box. A cut-out with a soft contact shadow stands directly on the page ground, about 300px tall, four columns. Centred 14px spec and 16px bold name below. One sticker or a slight rotation carries personality. Needs a clean render and a tinted or cream page.

name: shelf-baseline-row
what_you_see: Objects of different heights stand on one shelf line. 3-5 columns, 24-40px gutters, no tile, items aligned to the bottom of the image cell with a soft book shadow. Centred caption: 12px tag, 12-25px title, price. A count or 'Show All' outline button closes it. Ideal for books and bottles.

name: seam-contact-sheet
what_you_see: Four 3:4 images butted with 1px gaps on 24px page margins, or full bleed with 4px gaps, no card chrome. Model and still-life tiles mix under one studio ground. Captions sit on the page below at 12px, inset 12px. Ends in one small black 'show more'. Reads as a printed contact sheet.

name: product-stage-chapters
what_you_see: No grid at all. Each product gets one viewport on its own ground, black or grey or a colour per line, product centred, a tiny 9-12px mono label bottom-left, two buttons at most. Scroll steps between stages, with a small index to jump. For catalogues under about 12 products.

name: quiet-text-filter
what_you_see: Filtering set as plain text. One centred 32px serif sentence of comma-separated categories, or ALL and STYLE at 13px on a rule one tile wide, or 12px header links with the active one underlined. For editorial sites and small catalogues under 30 items. Never for large ranges.

name: colourway-stage
what_you_see: One object as a theatre set. Product centred or diagonal at 430-700px on a ground that changes with each colourway. Neighbours sit either side as low-alpha outlines with only the dial or blade coloured. Selected colour named beside small dots. PREVIOUS and NEXT at the edges in 12px mono. One clear action.

name: enquiry-spec-block
what_you_see: No price, no cart. Per piece: 14px description, then a 'Dimensions' label indented about 60px with figures beneath. Set in an index column beside a tall photograph, one enquiry link at the end. Fits antiques, furniture, architecture and made-to-order, where the conversation is the sale.

name: sticky-visual-configurator
what_you_see: For considered purchases. Left a sticky 870x560 stage, radius 20, one tone off the page. Right a 330px column of steps, each a 28px heading with dark lead and muted continuation, over option tiles radius 12. Later steps stay dimmed until the earlier ones are chosen. Dot progress on the right edge.

name: headline-with-inline-objects
what_you_see: Two-line 72-80px centred headline with small real objects set inside the line at x-height: a photo chip, a clock, a calendar slot, a selection box round one word. Objects are 56-64px tall, radius 12-16, and carry product truth. One or two per headline, no more.

name: giant-type-over-image
what_you_see: Image full viewport, one title at 15-20vw, line-height 0.8, tracking -0.05em, touching or crossing the margins, bottom-anchored, two lines offset left and right. No veil. Only a tiny 12px nav and one 32px outlined action hung above the second line. For culture, fashion, model launches.

name: designed-bottom-edge
what_you_see: Image has a composed end instead of a rectangle: fades into page colour at the fold so the portrait has no base, or clips to a 120px bottom radius on a brand field, or a cut-out building sits on paper. Lockup bottom-left, actions bottom-right on one baseline.

name: panel-diptych
what_you_see: Two full-height panels edge to edge at exactly 720px each, or a 480px central photo column with text in the side thirds. Zero gutter. One word or wordmark sits exactly on the seam. Panels can act as a chooser, one link per panel. No headline needed.

name: colour-wash-from-one-side
what_you_see: Solid brand colour covers the left 40% of a video or photo and fades to clear by 55%, or the image fades left into grainy near-black. Copy sits on the solid part with full contrast. More honest than a scrim, and it carries identity. Grain stops banding.

name: image-with-caption-only
what_you_see: Viewport-filling image with no headline. Text no larger than 30px: a caption bottom-left or a centred title, small nav, nothing else. Only for images strong enough to be the message: portfolios, fashion, architecture. Add a thin scroll cue so it does not look unfinished.

name: contained-plate
what_you_see: Image held back from the edges by a wide paper margin: 960px plate with caption row below, 75% viewport inset plate, or a 1400px photo starting ~500px down under a ghost wordmark. Copy lives on paper, never on the image, so no scrim is ever needed.

name: graphic-plate
what_you_see: Full-width crafted non-photo image in place of a picture: dithered bitmap landscape, stipple grain dunes, one giant flat-faceted brand ribbon ~1300px wide, or the product blurred huge at 30 degrees. Copy left or centred in its calm zone. Single rule-framed plate 700px tall works well.

name: paragraph-headline
what_you_see: Headline as a sentence-long paragraph: 48px weight 300 at 1.15-1.2 leading, 4 lines, first sentence ink, the rest ~60% ink, crossing a ribbon so type takes its hue. 14px live counter above, 44-48px CTA pair below, logo row between hairlines at the fold.

name: type-over-one-field
what_you_see: One large flat or soft shape behind centred type, and the type overprints it: 660px stepped brand glyph, 1050px white disc in a blurred colour field, or a floor glow. Headline 100-140px, line-height 0.85-1.05, button pair. No knockout, no shadow. The shape is the only decoration.

name: statement-with-annotation
what_you_see: One sentence, 48-92px, on paper colour, with a single hand-drawn stroke on one or two words: wobbly underline, ring, 3px accent. Stroke is an SVG path, not a CSS underline. ~160px of clear space above and below. Real tiles or line art rise at the fold.

name: statement-above-rising-media
what_you_see: Headline at one third height, then deliberate emptiness, then a real image or card entering at y 720-840, cut by the fold. Copy sits off-axis or centred at 56-88px. Top two thirds nearly bare, bottom edge rich. Scrolling is the reward. Faint grid may fade between them.

name: typographic-construction
what_you_see: Type used as structure: two 140px caps lines justified between 1px rules with a mark in the gap, words stacked into a stepped pyramid, or a small letter beside a 318px word. Small intro, thumbnail and link below on a strict grid.

name: quiet-paragraph
what_you_see: No headline size at all. A 19px paragraph or lettered list starting at y~270 under a 40px avatar and 14px name, or 12-16px text top-left at a 10-18px inset. Confidence by refusal. Portfolios, labs and archives only. Line length and tone carry everything.

name: type-split-by-prints
what_you_see: Giant 200px word split in two lines left and right, with 3-4 overlapping 400-530px prints stacked at centre covering the middle letters. The eye completes the word. Black on white, archival images, a small caption and date row at the base.

name: single-image-stage
what_you_see: One 576x720 image centred on off-white, ~90px from the top, name above, two-line caption below, six 3px progress dots. Reads as a gallery wall with one thing on it. For portfolios and curated sites whose next image is the interaction.

name: scattered-prints
what_you_see: ~10 unrotated portrait prints 150x205, no borders, scattered with wide gaps round a centred 30px wordmark, bottom row bleeding off, rising at different scroll rates. Or 3-4 crops ~325px wide staggered with two caps phrases. Photos are the only colour. Spacing must feel placed.

name: object-interleaved-with-type
what_you_see: Object sits between layers of type: ~275x520 can with one word passing behind and one in front, 800px server over a 260px ghost marquee, chrome figure overlapping bio text. Requires real depth ordering. Expressive and brand launches.

name: spotlit-object-on-dark
what_you_see: Pure black, device rising from bottom centre ~510px wide, back-lit, floor glow in the lower corners falling to black, one saturated element as the only colour. No headline, or a 90px line above. Lighting is the entire design. Needs a genuinely good render.

name: search-as-navigation
what_you_see: Search or a single question is the hero, for sites people come to find something in: 85px band with 24px placeholder, 42-56px pill search with filter chips, two cards with search and date, or a lone 1px underline prompt. No marketing claim.

name: pinned-panel-scroll-column
what_you_see: Viewport splits 40/60 on a 1px rule. Left panel stays fixed with logo, headline, actions and footer links; right column scrolls as a document. Panel needs a resident object. Also 50/50 colour panel with scrolling plates, or 1044px canvas with 348px side sheet.

name: staggered-hung-images
what_you_see: Images never share a row: two 580px images with tops offset 180px, then widths change to 553, 453 and 933 centred, left edges stepping x=100, 760, 252. Gaps 120-200px, caption under each. Two objects per viewport for commerce, one for a gallery.

name: bleed-side-alternation
what_you_see: Each section changes which edge the photo bleeds from: widths 700, 852, 816, or 42% of the viewport, with the text's left edge jumping to match and 260px of ground between. Photos start partway down the previous block, so the page descends as a staircase.

name: interlocked-panels
what_you_see: 706px image and 660px flat panel overlap: panel starts 65px below the image top and covers its right edge, with a stepped tab on one top corner. Rows swap sides. Hard corners, no shadow. Or photos hanging 290px past offset colour blocks.

name: seam-straddling-object
what_you_see: An image or card row starts on one ground and overlaps about 140px into the next, offset from the copy column. It joins two sections and gives depth with no shadow. A first card row can rise 40px over a hero's bottom edge.

name: opposite-margin-axis
what_you_see: Headline at the left 32px margin and action at the right 32px margin, on one horizontal axis at y=450 of a full-bleed image. The subject fills the span between. The same layout repeats on every screen.

name: solid-colour-statement
what_you_see: The page's only saturated field: full bleed, one viewport tall, 64px two-line sentence bottom left, nothing else. Add grain or a dissolving edge and let dark product shots overlap its top and bottom edges, or it reads as a flat poster.

name: pinned-photo-card-over
what_you_see: Full-bleed photo pinned at 100vh while a 770px flat card scrolls up over it, holding small eyebrow, 40px heading, lede, action and a second image. Text never sits on the photo. Hold for one or two viewports.

name: framed-single-screen
what_you_see: White page, 15px frame, 56px header row and 60px footer row hold all text; one 1410x780 photo fills between. Page height equals the viewport, so nothing scrolls away.

name: image-over-colour-seam
what_you_see: A 1360x698 photo, radius 8, centred across the join between a colour band and the page, the band ending 40% down the image. Gives the colour change depth without shadows.

name: stepped-section-edge
what_you_see: Full-bleed section with a non-straight top: left third rises 80px, centre recessed, right third 20px higher, hard 90-degree steps at x=326 and x=1070. Replaces any wave or gradient. Repeat the step in panels so it is a system.

name: single-measure-column
what_you_see: One centred 580-640px column for everything: bio, rows, media. On 1440 that is x=400-1040. Index rows split it into three columns at 224 pitch. Optional 1px dashed side rules and 48px inner padding. Pages often under 1600px tall.

name: column-with-one-side-bleed
what_you_see: All text and rails start at x=230 on a 980px column. Galleries start on that line and bleed only rightward past the viewport, scrolling sideways, so the left edge stays one line down the page. The next image peeks in to signal scroll.

name: one-light-one-grade
