what_you_see: Fix one time of day, one light direction, one colour bias across every subject, so warm-cool spread stays under 10 even if brightness swings. Crop to two ratios at most. Lift blacks 7-9%, hold highlights under 96%, saturation about 70%. Dusk amber for drama, matte daylight for calm.

name: palette-tied-set
what_you_see: Shoot on the page palette: ground, wardrobe and props drawn from its neutrals and accent. Grade seamless backgrounds to within 2-4% of the page colour so edges melt. One image per viewport or one-row colour story, flat frontal framing, no text on images, no borders.

name: studio-seamless-object
what_you_see: One object on one coloured seamless, single soft key from one side, long soft shadow, shallow focus. Object fills about 50% of tile width, same scale across all tiles. Every tile shares one tone range. Ground colour carries the identity; no props unless they repeat.

name: macro-material-crop
what_you_see: Crop tighter than feels safe: object cut by the frame on two sides, texture left unretouched. Natural side light, square corners or one 12-20px radius across the set. Alternate macro with one frontal or wide frame for scale. No overlay, no caption inside the image.

name: contrast-pairing
what_you_see: Plan images in pairs: neighbours contrast in tone or scale, never subject. Black-and-white grain beside saturated studio colour, macro beside wide, dark tile diagonal to light tile. Butt frames with 0-2px gaps. Photography supplies all page colour. No scrims, no filters.

name: scrimless-campaign-plate
what_you_see: Edge-to-edge or 20-32px radius panel. Subject composed to one side, copy on the open dark area at the page gutter, no scrim. Zone luminance spread under 0.04; white contrast at least 7 for body, 3.5 for 30px-plus display. If the zone fails, change the frame.

name: uncropped-native-plate
what_you_see: Native ratio, no radius, shadow, tint or inner caption. Fix one dimension: height up to 720px for a sequence, or a 330-420px column with unequal heights for an index. Interface stays neutral so all colour comes from the work. Caption below, 13px, centred or left.

name: dimensioned-technical-drawing
what_you_see: 1px grey wireframe at about 330px with centre lines, arrowed extension lines and rotated 12px mono dimensions, then cross-fade to the real object at identical position and scale. Or a large axonometric with neighbours pale and only the project tinted. Real dimensions only.

name: tonal-contour-field
what_you_see: Flat tinted panel, five to seven wandering lines one step lighter, 4-6px wide, running off every edge, never crossing, no closed loops. Isolines of warped noise plus a directional ramp. One field per tile. Keep type off it, or on a solid chip.

name: hand-inked-line
what_you_see: Strict structure, slight tremor: 1.25-2px near-black line, 60-100px, pale filled nodes or patches as the only tone, at most one flat colour. Let the drawing encode meaning, such as branches multiplying per tier. Keep to margins, tiles and emblems, never behind text.

name: stipple-engraving
what_you_see: One or two inks. Stippled plates about 600px with edges dissolving by grain into the ground, unframed, one per product; or 100px ink heads, colour kept in nearby labels. Same grain and palette across the series. Reuse as crest, avatar or watermark. Use real or public-domain sources.

name: machined-on-black
what_you_see: Pure black ground, no floor, no glow. Thin grazing strip lights plus dim soft boxes, satin metal at roughness about .38, knurling, bevels and micro-lettering. Long lens, 22-degree field. One object or a tight rhythm about 800px wide. One hue on one element only.

name: matte-clay
what_you_see: One matte tone over everything, soft even light, visible ambient occlusion, no texture. About 650px object on a bare same-tone ground, rotating with scroll, or a full clay scene with faint labels. Small coloured mono labels are the only colour.

name: wireframe-to-solid
what_you_see: A 3D part rotates, then flips to line art at exactly the same position, scale and angle as the section ground changes. One moment per page. Use an edge pass or two registered images.

name: exploded-part-view
what_you_see: Parts separated along one axis with equal gaps, lit from above, one soft shadow under the last part. Small numbered black dots on near-white, with the numbered specification in small caps below. Or silver plates with one accent plate, about 280px, reused as one object family.

name: macro-crop-render
what_you_see: Object about 1000px wide cropped by its tile, no device frame, tilted about 20 degrees, lit from upper left so every small form casts a shadow. Micro-grain, legible lettering. Copy-free chapter, or sits straight on a grain-filled tile.

name: material-story-render
what_you_see: One material truth, lit for it: ribbed knit under soft even light with no cast shadow, base fading into the page; or matte black hardware where labels supply all colour, tumbling 30-40 degrees; or a glossy floor with a long reflection. UI may sit on the reflection.

name: texture-first-loop
what_you_see: Make footage nearly abstract: heavy horizontal motion blur, faces never sharp, or slow macro in near black with one edge light. One saturated note at most. Radius 16 in a panel or full 100vh. Type or a translucent UI card sits directly on it, no scrim.

name: one-brand-object-moves
what_you_see: Headline and buttons are static from first paint. One owned object performs for 2-4s: a pixel glyph draws along its outline, a signal travels a connector, a wordmark rises behind a roofline. Nothing else moves, so the load feels authored and costs almost nothing to run.

name: light-arrives-last
what_you_see: Type and layout are final first. Then only light changes: a render rises from a 25% pastel ghost to full saturation in about 1s, or a glow blooms in a corner over 2-3s, with no slide or scale. The page feels lit rather than loaded.

name: focus-pull
what_you_see: Hero photo starts at 24-40px blur over a colour sampled from it and sharpens over 1-2s, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), while copy is already readable or fades in with it. Works like a lens racking, and it makes a slow image load look deliberate.

name: wordmark-docks-to-nav
what_you_see: Wordmark centred on a flat screen holds about 1s, then a single element travels and shrinks into its nav slot over 0.8-1.2s on cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1) while the panel behind lifts away. The page is already in place underneath. Use FLIP so one object makes the whole trip.

name: word-ink-scrub
what_you_see: Statement of 34-72px starts at 15-20% ink. Each word or character reaches full ink tied to scroll position, never to time, with a soft front 1-2 characters wide or a gradient spread over about 3 lines at reading height. Pace follows the reader. One per page, or one per chapter.

name: pinned-photo-dissolve
what_you_see: One full-height frame pins while photographs cross-dissolve at the same framing, with a 12px caption block holding bottom-left. Nothing slides. Chapters change by dissolve rather than by page movement, so a long story reads as a slow film. Three to five stills of matching exposure.

name: window-opens-to-full
what_you_see: A contained window pins and scales with scroll, about 750px wide to 2x, until it crops at the panel edge and UI text reads huge. Set transform-origin on the focal point, stop the scrub about a quarter early so the end holds, and avoid will-change, which blurs text.

name: section-theme-shift
what_you_see: Page background, type, rules and nav interpolate together between sections, for example paper to near-black over about half a viewport, with the CTA staying bright above the shift. No wipe and no edge. The colour change is the transition, so the page acts as one surface.

name: before-after-collapse
what_you_see: The section argues by scrub: pinned, a scattered collage of the old way (receipts, forms, emails with dashed links) fades to pale wireframe as the heading swaps and one clean window remains. Or a scene flips to wireframe for a data chapter. Motion carries the claim itself.

name: exploded-teardown
what_you_see: One pinned 3D subject or layered diagram is scrubbed apart: lid, board and base separate about 250px along dotted guides, or panes fan in perspective. Ground steps tone between chapters, and only copy and the object change. Prerender frames or use a real model. Worth it only for a physical product.

name: companion-object
what_you_see: One object stays on screen across several sections and changes as you scroll: a mark rotates 20 then 45 degrees, a phone swaps its screen, a model re-skins per project. Copy passes beside it. One object carries the story, so sections stop restarting.

name: layers-cross
what_you_see: Layering links two sections with no fade: a large heading holds still while a 400-580px video card scrolls across it, lifted by one wide shadow, about 0 24px 60px at 20%. Keep the fixed layer legible when covered, and let the top layer exit under the nav.

name: row-expands
what_you_see: Only the hovered row opens: height grows from about 19-177px to 240-460px, pushing later rows down while the others collapse into strips. 0.5s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1). An index becomes a gallery. Needs a stable pointer path, so give a row no neighbour that jumps under the cursor.

name: camera-move-demo
what_you_see: The camera does the storytelling: the demo opens zoomed hard into a prompt at about 100px type, then pulls back to the whole builder, or a full window pushes in 3x until one button fills the panel. Attention lands exactly where the claim is. Use for one hero only.

name: schematic-traffic
what_you_see: The product is drawn as a diagram that runs: packets pass through a band, cards change state at a scan line, or speech flows along a ribbon into a capsule and leaves polished. Confined to one band under the nav, so it never competes with the headline.

name: in-place-swap
what_you_see: The frame never moves. Title and still cross-swap in the same position, so only image and words change. Duration 0.3-0.6s. The quietest transition that still feels authored, because the layout itself is the constant.

name: dissolving-window
what_you_see: Window or shell with 1px line and radius 16-24 dissolves into the page: mask the lower third, or the right and bottom edges, to page colour. Text stays real and dims with distance. No hard base, no shadow halo, no fake window edge.

name: chromeless-product-canvas
what_you_see: No window. A tinted panel about 845px wide is the app: oversized search line in display type, a hairline, then 4 masonry columns of 170px with a 16px gap mixing photos, quotes, highlighted notes and price tags.

name: frozen-interaction
what_you_see: One menu or dialog at 1-2x over its app faded to 30%: 392px white menu, radius 12, soft shadow, selected row filled with a 2px accent bar, shortcut chips. A large cursor rests on the row. Keycaps may overlap the edge.

name: embedded-working-product
what_you_see: Real working UI inline with no frame: a 1136px search with four selects, a count and a pager; or 52x76 date chips with masked ends; or a typed block with a caret. Full size, keyboard reachable, and it must work on a phone.

name: single-control-enlarged
what_you_see: One real control scaled 1.5-2x inside a tile and cropped by its edge: a pill, keycap or field with a click ring and cursor. Frosted white fields, radius 14, or about 100px of air each side if uncropped. No window.

name: one-bright-line
what_you_see: Code panel cropped by the card edge on the left 43%, top-right radius 20, 1px top highlight. 11px language tabs. Every line at 25% ink except the single method line at full ink. Serves as texture with one readable point.

name: single-claim-line
what_you_see: One line 1.5-2px, optional fill fading to near-white, four ring markers or a live end dot, hairline grid, 12px axis labels, caption half accent, half ink. Width up to 1130px. Or a word set large over the line.

name: one-filled-shape
what_you_see: Descending isometric bars in 1px dotted outline on black, no axes, with only the winner solid and labelled in accent. Or a greyscale diagram with one dark outline, or a 230px outline pie with one accent slice.

name: margin-between-two-lines
what_you_see: 2px line with end dot over a dotted 1px line, fine vertical hatching filling only the gap between them. 12px legend at the base, one baseline rule, no axes or gridlines. No colour needed.

name: inked-map
what_you_see: Regions in 2px ink outline on a pale blob, one highlighted with 8% fill, white card with region name and price. Or a dark map with numbered clusters and a search overlay, radius 12.

name: focus-pull-on-code
what_you_see: Black code window, every line blurred except one, with that token highlighted and a floating type hover card in 14px mono with a hairline. The blur moves line to line, like a focus pull.

name: scrubbable-slow-motion
what_you_see: A sentence appears word by word on a rule with per-token numbers under it, a candidates list beside it, and a scrubber labelled 30x slowed down, from Detailed to Realtime.

name: cost-bars
what_you_see: Cost difference shown as length: rival a full-width bar with its price, yours a 12px dot or a short bar. 12 to 32px bar height, 22px tabular prices right-aligned, a row of shared assumptions above and small-print method below. Use only with honest, sourced numbers.

name: single-plan-leaders
what_you_see: One plan as a 416px card under a Yearly/Monthly pill: 16px item left, dotted leader, right-aligned 13px mono caps status, either included or a dated promise. Full-width 48px button below. Reads like a receipt, so the honest 'coming soon' line builds trust.

name: usage-calculator
what_you_see: Price set by the reader: slider with 1M, 10M and 50M ticks or an inline select per plan, boxed value, per-unit rate, and a bar reading 'Estimated total' with a button. Prices update live with no layout shift. For metered products where a flat tier table would mislead.

name: open-document-faq
what_you_see: No accordion. Every answer open in a 670px left-aligned column: 22px display questions, 16/26 body, 34px between pairs, real links, a 20px hash anchor appearing in the left margin on hover. Searchable with cmd-F and linkable. Needs answers worth reading and suits developer tools.

name: oversized-button-close
what_you_see: The button is the design: centred 64 to 80px headline, muted line, then a 64 to 72px button, radius 18 to 20, 24 to 32px bold label, or a giant 750px pill holding the whole line. Add ratings or a checklist beneath. Say one thing.

name: hero-reprise-close
what_you_see: The end rhymes with the start: repeat the hero mark, panel, icon shape or slogan at a new scale. A 590px faded squircle echoing the app icon, a ghost logo bleeding off a corner, or the hero stack again. Quiet, and needs no new art.

name: photo-sign-off
what_you_see: Closing on a real photograph or film: full bleed or a 1376px card at radius 32, 48 to 120px white heading placed in the image's own shadow, 16 to 22px copy, one white pill. Use a local scrim. Repeat the hero's world so the page closes a loop.

name: half-width-card-close
what_you_see: A 540px left-aligned card of dark grain lit from one side, radius 12, white mark, 36/39 heading, small white button. The right half of the row stays empty, so the close reads as a placed object rather than a band. Sits just above a matching dark footer.

name: giant-type-sign-off
what_you_see: Display type carries the ending: 100 to 250px flush left, leading under 1, a last word in accent or underlined, install block or field small beside it. On a black band or field. Keep a sharp scale contrast with something tiny next to it.

name: link-rows-close
what_you_see: The close is a stack of links, not a band. Up to 110px lines filling the width, each with a thin chevron flush right, or 52px bar buttons with mono caps, or a 68px strip of numbered links. Navigation becomes type. Use when several next steps are equal.

name: composer-close
what_you_see: The last call to action is the product: centred 48px heading, then a real 54 to 62px input, up to 766px wide, radius 14, with its action inside. Prompt box, URL field, file drop or preset amounts. Starts the first task instead of describing it.

name: seam-overlap-close
what_you_see: The close physically joins the footer: the page plate, inset 52px from one side, ends in a 50px corner and reveals colour beneath, or a white card straddles the seam, or the footer overlaps a grain band. Depth with no shadow, and the page reads as one object.

name: signature-art-close
what_you_see: One owned drawing fills half the band: extruded ribbons, a dithered ASCII tree, a chrome wordmark, overlapping lens circles, tilted slab. Heading and pill on the other side. It must be made for this brand and appear earlier on the page, or it reads as decoration.

name: contact-as-headline
what_you_see: The contact detail is the headline: a 48px phone number on a 90px strip, or a 76px email address in the page's display type, with no button. For agencies, local trades and voice products, where one action really is a call or an email.

name: media-plate-then-caption
what_you_see: Three or four columns, 8 to 32px gaps. A plate 286 to 500px tall holding a real fragment or photo cropped by its edge, then 24px of space, a 20 to 28px/400 title and 16/1.4 copy at 58% ink on the bare page. No card, border or shadow behind the text.

name: poster-tiles
what_you_see: Two tiles per row, 8 to 16px gaps, near full bleed, little or no radius. Centred stack in the top third: 40/44 title, one line, pills or chevron links. Product fills the lower 55 to 60%, art-directed per tile, some cropped at the base. Pair a light tile with a dark one.

name: bleed-past-the-edge
what_you_see: A 265 to 360px copy column beside an 830px window or photo that passes the container and runs off the viewport edge, saying there is more. Add four 70px-pitch icon rows for spec detail. Use once or twice for the most important product moment.

name: viewport-chapters
what_you_see: Consecutive 100vh sections, no dividers. A 430px text block sits in the empty part of each photo at a 100px margin, moving per shot: 48px heading, three lines of 16px, one ghost button. Needs at least three strong images. Flat colour scenes around one object also work.

name: typographic-index
what_you_see: The list is the design: names 28 to 100px on 1px rules or none, active full ink, others 25 to 55%, a small preview swapping beside the list. A progress line can fill the active rule. For services and channels with good names, in agency and bold brand pages.

name: list-drives-pinned-stage
what_you_see: A 444 to 672px list beside a sticky 584 to 800px stage, three to five steps at about 72vh each. Scroll sets the active step, time plays the change. Active full ink, others 30%, plus one bar or rule. Stage must stay full. Plain flow without JavaScript.

name: pinned-chapter-stage
what_you_see: A pinned screen with a fixed skeleton where only contents change across three to seven chapters: a 100vh film with a foot caption on the emptier side, a shared rule, a time rail of ticks, or a stage flooded per product beside an 88px icon rail.

name: stacked-sheets
what_you_see: Sheets about 1248 by 560px, radius 16, sticky at a top offset growing 14px per sheet so edges peek, shadow 0 30px 40px at 28% black. 72px left padding, 48px title, 20/30 copy, UI with a dark rail bleeding off the right. Three to six peers, block flow.

name: split-pinned-half
what_you_see: A 50/50 split: one half pins a panel or photo with copy at its foot while the other scrolls macro, model and detail shots, or rows on 1px rules that swap the pinned photo. Fill can step lighter per image. For one product or person with several images.

name: scrubbed-statement
what_you_see: Type as the event, once per page: a pinned pale section where three 64px lines arrive from 8px blur and low opacity above three 70px step cards, or a 3D form inside a ring of 120 ticks filling with progress. For a positioning statement.

name: steps-showing-the-real-thing
what_you_see: Three or four columns, each a small marker, a 32px tight title, 18/29 copy, then the real screen at full size with no window chrome: a picker, a form, a feed. Reserve copy height so the proofs start level. The first thing to try for any product.

name: colour-flood-footer
what_you_see: One full-bleed field of the brand colour, the largest flat colour on the page, held back until the end. All text in one tint of that field: white, or a dark of the same hue. Serif or display heads, 13-14px links, one lighter rule inset 16px. No second colour.

name: giant-wordmark-finish
what_you_see: Links on top, then the wordmark at full container width as the very last thing, 220-380px tall, in full contrast, framed by hairlines. Use a trimmed SVG or size from ink bounds so it meets both margins exactly. Never stretch glyphs. Only a thin legal row may follow.

name: masked-wordmark
what_you_see: Edge-to-edge wordmark used as a window: halftone photo, moving video or customer imagery shows through the letters, or the letters are 1-1.5px outline with no fill. Use background-clip text or an SVG mask. The image must be busy enough to keep the letters readable at a glance.

name: statement-closer
what_you_see: The footer's largest element is a sentence, 76-170px, not a logo: a mission line, a repeat of the hero heading, or a plain ask. Small link columns or one legal row sit around it. Say something true and specific, or it reads as a slogan.

name: final-image-footer
what_you_see: No separate block. The last photo or film runs to the page bottom and the footer is one row laid inside it: 12px tracked links, a round back-to-top, copyright right. The page ends on a picture. Needs a dark, quiet lower edge in the image, or a scrim drawn from it.

name: rhythm-rows
what_you_see: Rows change count on purpose: one full tile, then two, then three, all locked to the same gutters. Square corners, 20-50px gaps, 55px page margin or less. No hover chrome. The change of beat replaces any need for cards, and it looks curated rather than generated.

name: true-ratio-gallery
what_you_see: Each work keeps its own proportions, uncropped. Set a max width per column, align the images to the bottom of the row so tops stagger and titles share one baseline, or centre them on the row midline. For art, architecture and anything where a crop would be a lie.

name: dense-image-wall
what_you_see: Edge to edge, 0-10px gaps, no captions, four to nine columns, and the page is simply the work. Fills the viewport so scale itself is the statement. Works for archives, community output and templates. Add a fade at the base if the wall is truncated, with one button on it.

name: fixed-height-filmstrip
what_you_see: A horizontal band where every image has one fixed height and its own native width: 620px tall, widths 300-900, 100px gaps, white above and below. Driven by wheel or drag. Height is the only constant, so mixed work sits together without a crop.

name: pinned-project-stage
what_you_see: One viewport holds one project; scroll swaps it in place. A centred 500-1170px frame stays pinned while neighbours enter from the edges, or a smaller clip rises over a large frame. Keep the swap under one screen of scroll, and give phones a plain stacked version.

name: single-file-spine
what_you_see: Every project in one narrow column on the centre axis or a rail, images at natural ratio about 434-580px wide, 26-120px apart, no sections or headings. Name and place in a small column beside each. The length of the list is the proof.

name: narrowing-filmstrip
what_you_see: Active tile 818x460, then strips narrowing to about 188, 90, 42 and 8px, all the same height, radius 6, gap 16. Next stories compress at the edge, so depth is shown in one row. 40px arrow tiles top right, a white 40px title on the art. Stack on phones.

name: designed-cover-system
what_you_see: No stock photos: every post gets a cover from one system. Dotted field with a logo plate, line sketch with one accent, lettered cartoon or typographic poster. One rule, one palette, generated per post. It turns a feed into a publication, and is the cheapest way to look art-directed.

name: map-as-figure
what_you_see: The map is a drawn figure, not an embed: pale land on one tone, radius 32, flat pins, and 1px lines rising to 24px city labels at staggered heights, with 'HQ' as a small outline chip and upcoming sites in grey. Say something a Google embed cannot.

name: centred-menu-column
what_you_see: One centred column about 420-700px on warm paper: 16px tracked caps name, 17px italic ingredients beneath, price inline or on its own line, script or caps section heads, a small OR between choices. Reads as the printed card on the table. For fine dining and prix fixe.

name: running-text-index
what_you_see: A catalogue as text: all items as a list of 14-56px names, some with a year in brackets, the current item's caption beneath, one image at a time beside it. Or huge condensed service names on a 54px pitch with arrows pinned far right. Reads as an inventory.

name: scene-per-product
what_you_see: Each product gets a whole viewport: full-bleed colour or illustrated scene, about 620px art, a 72px title, a 12px caps two-liner, one button, an index badge and a small pager. For ranges of four to eight with real character. Always show a plain list view as well.

name: hanging-quote-on-grid
what_you_see: No card. Two columns on the page grid, 32/40 quote at weight 500, tracking -2%, opening mark hung left of the text edge so the text stays on the grid. Name and role pinned to the base at 14px, customer logo right-aligned on that line. Pair one long quote with one four-word quote.

name: display-pull-quote
what_you_see: One quote as a full-width moment: 48 to 64px on 1.05 leading, tracking -2 to -3%, often the page's only serif, 700 to 1220px wide. Mark in the left rail or none. Attribution 14 to 18px below, with square portrait and logo split by a rule. Sits between hairlines or on a quiet field.

name: quiet-interlude-quote
what_you_see: A short centred quote between feature blocks, no card: 20 to 28px, 580 to 820px wide, 36 to 48px avatar, 14px name and role, optional logo after a 1px divider. Emphasis by ink: first sentence full ink and the rest muted, or one phrase at weight 500. Stays below headings in weight.

name: colour-flood-quote
what_you_see: One or two panels of loud colour on a quiet page: radius 8 to 40, 400 to 800px tall, 24 to 36px quote with tight leading top left, name and logo pinned low. Unequal widths such as 880 and 432 beat equal ones. Text in a dark tint of the fill. Use once.

name: letter-or-interview
what_you_see: One person at length. A 766px square paper card with 48px avatar, ruled heading, 16/28 candid bullets and a signature. Or a full-screen question and answer split by 1px rules, one exchange per viewport. Use when you have a real voice and no logos.

name: quote-beside-interaction
what_you_see: A review shares a row with something the reader can do: two 546 by 600 cards, 8px gap, radius 24, one a 44px question with 54px pill answers, the other stars, 44/48 quote and a member chip. Proof sits one tap from the decision. Keep legal disclosures visible.

name: logos-inside-another-block
what_you_see: No band. Five 20 to 24px grey marks in the text column under the sentence they support, at 86px centres; or a 94px strip on the hero's foot; or a 450 by 56 dock; or marks passing behind the headline. Proof attaches to a claim.

name: typeset-client-names
what_you_see: Client names as type, no logos. Three rows of 51px serif at 120px height on 1px rules, 18px hollow circles between, rows sliding opposite ways. Or an alphabetical 14px list in one 480px column, where a gallery and a global brand weigh the same.

name: figure-ledger
what_you_see: Stats as stacked rows. Right 600px column beside a 40px two-tone heading, rows 160px tall on 1px hairlines: 64/400 figure left, right-aligned 16px label over a 12px mono caps note. Or alternate figure, customer logo and one sentence on a dark band.

name: number-as-diagram
what_you_see: The figure is drawn, not stated: widths in true ratio (170 beside 988px for 45 and 220 wpm), bars proportional on the page grid, a dot matrix spelling the count, circles counted and crossed, or one hairline curve under 2px-ticked metrics. The scale must be honest.

name: sentence-stats
what_you_see: Numbers read as sentences. Centred 64/600 lines at 88px pitch: figure, an inline object at cap height replacing the word space, noun. Or 24px facts split by a rule, or bold figures opening ordinary lines beside a phone. No labels, no cards.

name: one-giant-number
what_you_see: One figure owns the section: 96 to 200px, tight, alone in a band or outlined card, 13 to 14px caption. It may roll on entry or change with scroll. Choose the one number that would surprise someone, and never rest on zero.

name: numerals-on-photo
what_you_see: White numerals 40 to 130px directly on a photo, 12 to 14px tracked label, darkening only where they sit. Inset the pane 100px or use the photo's dark area. Or small white chips at radius 10 on a close-up. The photo must relate to the number.

name: full-bleed-project
what_you_see: One image edge to edge, 740px or viewport tall, no radius, breaking the page margins. White caption bottom left at 32px inset: 15/500 name over 15px mono type. No scrim. Or fade the bottom third into the page and set logo and statement on the fade.

name: one-backdrop-portraits
what_you_see: Different people cut onto one ground: 170 to 320px portraits, radius 0 to 24, a single warm or neutral backdrop, 14 to 18px name, muted credentials. Separate headshots read as one shoot, even when taken years apart.

name: founder-bio-split
what_you_see: One named person as the pitch. 50/50: a 676 by 1000 greyscale portrait cropped to the waist beside a bio in the page's display serif at 63/68, link pinned to the photo's base. Or a 56px greeting on ink beside an offset-framed portrait.

name: authored-portraits
what_you_see: Portraits in one commissioned hand: black-line busts on a 1px rule with skin as the only fill, hatched circles on a dotted bus line, or depth-of-field overlap with the focused face sharp. The treatment is the signature.

name: regular-weight-quiet
what_you_see: Headline at weight 400 only, 48-116px, line-height 1.0-1.1, tracking -0.01 to -0.03em, black or warm near-black, flush left, one line if it fits. Allow no bold heading anywhere on the page. Hierarchy comes from size and ink alone; labels drop to 11-13px mono or small caps.

name: quiet-serif-over-sans-ui
what_you_see: One serif used only for H1 and H2, weight 300-500, 44-80px (up to 128px on dark manifesto pages), line-height 1.0-1.1, tracking 0 to -0.03em, single ink, never bold. All UI, labels and body stay sans or mono, so the serif alone carries the voice.

name: same-size-two-voices
what_you_see: One size, 32-64px, weight 400-600, line-height 1.0-1.25, tracking 0 to -0.03em. Two clauses split by tone: first at full ink, second at 45-60% ink, on a second line or running on. Alternatives: drop weight two steps, or change case. This block replaces the subhead.

name: caps-block
what_you_see: Uppercase headline in a condensed or neo-grotesque cut, 56-120px, line-height 0.8-0.95, tracking 0 to -0.04em, short lines of near-equal length so the text locks into one block. Pair with thin sentence-case body at 16-20px. Reserve it for headlines, never nav or labels.

name: under-scaled-title
what_you_see: H1 at only 28-48px, weight 400-500, line-height 1.1-1.3, one or two lines, and nothing on the page is larger. On utility pages use one word at 48-64px with 90-120px of air above and below. Scale comes from images, tables or whitespace, never from the type.

name: statement-as-hero
what_you_see: A full sentence or list takes the headline job, 35-80px, weight 400-500, line-height 1.1-1.2, with no size or weight change inside it, running 60-100% of the container. Break lines by hand. Allow at most one inline object or underlined link. No subhead follows.

name: ink-then-grey-run-in
what_you_see: One paragraph at 32-48px, weight 300-500, line-height 1.0-1.2, left aligned, 780-1150px wide. First sentence in full ink, the rest runs on in the same line at about 6:1 contrast. No eyebrow, no subhead. Repeat for nearly every section. Use text-wrap: pretty, never balance.

name: anaphora-list
what_you_see: Five left-aligned lines in a centred block, each opening with the same short word in bold accent sans at about 54px, followed by a serif phrase at the same size, about 67px line step. Repetition turns a stance into the strongest type moment on the page.

name: line-on-image
what_you_see: One dry line at 20-48px placed in the clear area of a full-bleed photograph, 24px inset, with one 16px underlined link 24-30px below, black or white by image tone. No button, no scrim.

name: wordmark-masthead
what_you_see: Brand name fills the first screen edge to edge, 16-32px side margins, 130-300px tall, under or behind the nav. Let renders overlap it, or set it tone on tone near 1.1:1 as a watermark. The headline sits below at about a quarter of the size. Nav omits the logo.

name: full-width-statement
what_you_see: A short line scaled to fill the container: 135-318px, line-height 0.75-0.85, tracking -0.04 to -0.05em, alone in a plain viewport, or two lines force-justified to the margins. Once per page, as a section break or sign-off. Fit the size by measuring.

name: inline-objects-in-sentence
what_you_see: Headline at 45-80px with real objects in the line: photo chips, clock tiles, product cards, pills, about 1em tall, each a different shape, holding real content, radius 10-14px, 1px border, at most two per line. Raise line-height to 1.15-1.25 to clear them. The words alone must still be a sentence.

name: chapter-numeral-or-word
what_you_see: A chapter opener with a single year, word or set of initials at 300-920px wide, alone on a plain ground with only the nav remaining. Use between long sections. It may recolour per chapter.

name: highlight-strip-on-photo
what_you_see: Text lines each wrapped in a flat bright strip with 2px side padding, black text, bottom-left of a full-bleed slide. Use box-decoration-break: clone so padding repeats per line. It guarantees contrast over any photograph.
